# Flash Next batch MTP chaining receipt

The shared Metal adapter can submit a stream's kept-window absorb and all chained MTP drafts in one command buffer.
`FZ_BATCH_MTP_CHAIN=1` enables the experiment; it defaults to off. Streams still draft serially.
Each encoded step owns its CPU-written position, row and selector metadata. GPU score/key scratch remains shared.
The new buffers add 17,472 bytes of payload per session; admission still checks the actual process footprint.

## Qualified scope

TensorFold 1.0.5, upstream `bec00ae6961a43a9ab73c4fa9338c167b3f82851`;
inference source `6dbf17059a846f2c9c40a92c79b5558d41f2960f`.
The [manifest](manifest.json) pins the source tree, compiler archive and both executed binaries.
Rebuilt binaries match the hashes of the executed artifacts.

One 80-core M3 Ultra, 256 GiB RAM, macOS 26.7.1, system Metal, Zig 0.17.0 targeting `apple_m1`.
Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-6bit-MTP`, download metadata revision
`45032a193a5d4126ba8534822cbaf8fb30b3e368`.
Public fixtures have 23, 66, 2,764 and 11,237 prompt tokens, with thinking off and on.
The direct gate also uses the first 2,050 tokens of the longest fixture to cross into sparse selection during drafting.

## Correctness

[Checkpoint gate](checkpoint-gate.log):

- 180 paired comparisons at absorb widths 1/4/16, previous speculative tails 0/3, and draft depths 0/1/2/4/8/15.
  Draft tokens, final hidden-state bytes, head positions and pooled-block counts match serial drafting exactly.
  Wider absorbs use controlled repeated row inputs to exercise the head independently of the scheduler.
- Four 64-token replies match fresh legacy plain decoding in plain, serial-MTP and chained-MTP modes.
- All three modes pass cancellation, slot reuse, prompt admission, multi-chunk marks and prefix restoration with an active peer.
- [HTTP receipt](http.json): 96 responses across six blocks, four rounds each. Bodies, token fingerprints and usage match.
  Every four-slot block observes four active sessions. Prefix caching is disabled.

The executed HTTP helper is pinned to the inference-source commit.
The final helper additionally invalidates stale success before reading fixtures and rejects unobserved shared sessions.
Both failure cases were checked locally; the recorded run independently satisfies the strengthened parallelism gate.

## Timings

The checkpoint gate records one observation, including prefill and decode:

| Phase | Serial MTP | Chained MTP |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Draft calls | 84 | 84 |
| GPU waits during drafting | 256 | 84 |
| Draft time | 0.312223 s | 0.261944 s |
| Total group time | 12.473931 s | 12.375544 s |

Draft time fell 16.1%. This single observation does not establish a general speedup.

HTTP uses identical public requests, greedy decoding, a 16,384-token context and 128-token reply limit.
The one-slot control runs off/on. Four-slot blocks run off/on/on/off.
Each block has one excluded warmup and three measured rounds; every group emits 459 tokens.

| Parallel slots | Serial warm median | Chain warm median | Group throughput change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1, legacy control | 15.191969 s | 15.226884 s | -0.23% |
| 4, shared adapter | 14.599447 s | 14.496549 s | +0.71% |

These are end-to-end group timings, including prompt processing. They are not an isolated decode benchmark.
The effect is small; the option stays experimental. The one-slot driver does not consume the switch.

## Memory and cleanup

A [footprint sample](memory.json) from the final four-slot serial block reports a process-lifetime physical peak
of 186,421,791,496 bytes. This is not a whole-run peak across all server restarts.
System swap usage remained zero at the probes. One model process ran at a time under the existing admission lock.
The original service was restored and verified healthy; native test processes and the lock were removed.

## Host validation and limits

[Host check](host.log): 137/137 build steps succeed; 351 tests pass, two are skipped and none fail.
Other test steps are cached. Whole-tree `zig fmt --check build.zig zig` passes with Zig 0.17.0.
[Golden check](golden.log): 309 equal, 10 documented differences, zero unexpected differences.
Both native builds pass. The lean checker finds 542 inherited problems on upstream and candidate, with none added.
Astra reviewed the chain, the metadata lifetime, state accounting, direct gates and benchmark failure handling.

This receipt qualifies these fixtures on one M3 Ultra and this checkpoint.
CUDA, other Apple chips, other RAM classes/checkpoints, more than four sessions, 32K+ contexts,
separate cold-prefill sweeps, a previous-release comparison and a standard-server comparison were not run.
The patch is a shared-adapter scheduling change using the existing Metal operators and precision.

## Reproduce

Run on an idle GPU with no other model loaded and use the platform's admission lock and service restoration procedure.

```sh
zig build native tf-flashnext-batch -Dcpu=apple_m1 -Doptimize=ReleaseFast
FZ_N=64 zig-out/bin/tf-flashnext-batch "$MODEL" \
  docs/receipts/flashnext-mtp-chain-2026-10-10/prompts/{short,thinking,sparse,sparse-thinking}.json
python3 tools/zig/flashnext_mtp_chain.py \
  zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native "$MODEL" \
  docs/receipts/flashnext-mtp-chain-2026-10-10/prompts output --tokens 128 --rounds 4
zig build test test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig fmt --check build.zig zig
```
# Flash Next read-out cut-over at 128 rows

`TF_FLASHNEXT_READOUT_ROWS=128`, off by default, moves the HC read-out's switch to the prompt tiles from 64 to 128 rows. That adds
up to 7% throughput at 16 streams on a GB10. Any cut from 96 to 160 serves the same, so 128 is a value inside a flat range and
not a sharp optimum. These runs set the value at build time. On the same build with the switch unset and at 128, 16 streams,
`--reps 3`, a check gave +7.1%, +3.7%, +2.1% and 0.0%, the same order as below, and replies at 1, 4 and 16 streams were equal.

## Source and environment

- Baseline: main at `94b90c9db6`, one NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121), driver 580.159.03, kernel 6.17.0-1026-nvidia, aarch64.
- `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3`, `sha256:2140e699b3beaf7f96a0081fd9c9406bc3832b435cdb60dfa2d261f7d2f34a1c`; nvcc 13.3, V13.3.73, CUDA 13.3.
- Checkpoint `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-MLX-4bit-MTP`, revision `2b170fa6309d5d1ee380b35636075fac7945f286`.
- `tools/bench_concurrent.py`, fresh server per run, alternating builds over two cycles. `cells.csv` has every cell.

The cut-over runs use `--context 16384 --prompt-cache-gib 0 --parallel 16`, `--tokens 256 --reps 3`, `--temperatures 0,1.0`, 16
streams, four builds differing only in `readout_tile_rows`.

## The cut-over, served at 16 streams

End-to-end tok/s, mean of two cycles. 64 is main; 96 and 160 are the cuts either side of this change.

| Prompt | Temp | 64 | 96 | 128 | 160 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| code | 0 | 323.2 | 346.1 | 346.4 | 345.1 |
| chat | 0 | 277.0 | 287.4 | 287.7 | 287.8 |
| code | 1 | 206.4 | 213.5 | 213.5 | 213.4 |
| chat | 1 | 187.3 | 187.0 | 187.8 | 187.6 |

Cycles differ by at most 1.2 tok/s, except 64 at code, temp 1, by 3.2.

This compares cuts, not cells on either side of 128 rows. The tie from 96 to 160 suggests these 16-stream rounds stay below 96
rows, so those three columns take one path and the 64 column takes the other, on the same rounds. No served round at or above
128 rows was measured here, and Flash Next stops at 16 lanes. That side is unchanged: it takes the tiles under either value.

## Main against this branch

Short contexts, 1 to 16 streams, same run as #1739's receipt: 16 streams gain +7.4%, +3.9%, +2.5% and +0.2%, and every other
cell is within 0.5% of main. All token comparisons are equal. Long contexts show no difference beyond the noise in that receipt.

## The timing test disagrees, and the served runs decide

`tf-cuda-test flashnext-readout-cut` times the two paths directly, alternated, on one set of weights. There the tiles are about
twice as fast at every size from 32 to 256 rows: 1.60 ms against 4.21 ms at 128 rows. Served rounds show the opposite between 64
and 127 rows. That test repeats a read-out on warm weights while a served round reads each layer's in turn, which may be
the difference; this is not established. The 29.6 ms against 11.4 ms in the first version of #1741 came from an older
v1.1.7-based build's profile and could not be reproduced on main, so they are withdrawn.

## Not established

- Prompt chunks of 64 to 127 rows now take the row kernels too, and were not timed separately. First-token times at the short
  prompts here are within 2.3% of main, but those prompts are too short to reach that path.
- HIP and Metal do not use this path and were not run.
# gfx1151 cancellation follow-up

Measured on 2026-10-18, following the unresolved 27B case in [#994](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/994).
This is a fresh A/B run on public source `76aafcf274e60a5e31a59ce145b2f71f7b366e9d` and the runtime patch
in `5429554e708fdf7a9e0017301a00eb87a4182acd`. It is not a full release qualification.
Subsequent source changes shorten comments/docstrings for the lean rule; runtime and gate execution logic are unchanged.

The single GPU is a BOSGAME M5's Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`). The checkpoint is
`TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` at `70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f`.
All 17 checkpoint files match their previously pinned public Git-blob/LFS digests; see `checkpoint.json`.

## Cancellation result

The same gate runs three trials per build. Each trial separately measures the time from closing a long request's
socket until the engine's `requests_running` metric reaches zero, then the next short request sent 50 ms behind
another cancellation. Every long request uses a fresh nonce first, preventing long-prefix reuse.
The client closes 0.4 seconds after sending it. All twelve cancelled prompts fit within the 16,384-token window
and end with `reason=client-left`, zero emitted tokens. Actual prompt lengths are in `audit.json`.

| Measurement | Unmodified base | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Idle short baseline, best of three | 1.899 s | 1.913 s |
| Disconnect to idle metric, three trials | 4.720–4.744 s | 0.032–0.042 s |
| Next short request, three trials | 6.532–6.548 s | 1.902–1.907 s |
| Cancelled request lifetime, arrival to end | 5.08–5.14 s | 0.43–0.44 s |
| Gate: release <=0.5 s and short <=idle+0.5 s | **3/3 failed** | **3/3 passed** |

All fourteen short replies across the two builds have the same complete native token SHA-256:
`ad11ca37c7fcabaf13c8fc1142956890438c4ca49c58d6f579c3eef5485b77d5`.
`*-http.jsonl` retains each short request/response and each cancelled request's exact body.
`*-server.log` independently retains six client-left completions per build.
Arrival-to-end lifetime is not used as disconnect-to-release time.

The harness's optional `--baseline-27b` also prints the historical v1.0.12 receipt for comparison.
Those historical numbers are labelled separately; the table above is the fresh unmodified-versus-fixed comparison.

## Correctness and timing controls

An identical uncancelled 14,975-token prompt produces the same full native token SHA-256 on both builds:
`677caeac8d5e87f26c67e37ff1551667fc3217c4690d7a276204d22c2504f0a1`.
Prefill takes 79.021 s before and 78.867 s after. This is one timing control, not a broad performance claim.
The complete requests and replies are in `*-uncancelled.json`.

The unmodified `serve_check.py` then passes its 13 exercised comparisons on the fixed server, including
concurrent/solo and resumed/fresh checks. It prints 15 successes, but two drafting comparisons are unexercised:
this checkpoint has no draft head. The raw output retains all fifteen lines without inflating exercised coverage.

The host build passes 292/292 steps; cached results are reused. It reports 126 new passes and two skips, and the
HIP Qwen family reports 32 passes/one skip. Before the implementation, retaining the old 2,048-row threshold and
the null cancellation hook makes both new CPU regressions fail. Remaining work in that deliberately failing build
was stopped once those two failures were captured; it is not a completed full-suite run. See `cpu-*.log`.

## Reproduction and scope

`state.json` retains exact build/server/test commands and both binary SHA-256 values. Use Zig 0.17.0,
HIP 7.1 and clang 21; the HIP build targets `gfx1151` with explicit compiler/include/device-bitcode paths.
The server uses `--context 16384 --parallel 4 --prompt-cache-gib 1 --no-thinking --metrics-open` on loopback.
Run from each source version, using the same pinned checkpoint:

```sh
python3 zig/tests/qwen35/serve_cancel_release.py http://127.0.0.1:8092 amd-cancel-27b \
  --runs 3 --server-log SERVER_LOG --record HTTP_JSONL --baseline-27b
python3 zig/tests/qwen35/serve_check.py http://127.0.0.1:8092 amd-cancel-27b 64
```

Only single-rank HIP Qwen prompt passes of at least 512 rows now poll cancellation at layer boundaries.
Shorter passes still finish their current chunk; tensor-parallel groups retain between-chunk cancellation so
ranks do not diverge at a collective. This run does not qualify every prompt cut, other models, multi-GPU,
drafting, or all release gates. It does not implement DFlash2 or resolve the separate benchmark-publication work.

This directory is a separate sanitized publication copy. Machine-local paths/hostname are replaced with
placeholders and trailing whitespace normalized. Request/response values and native hashes are unchanged.
`publication.json` records source/published hashes; `SHA256SUMS` covers every published file except itself.
Original raw evidence and service-control state remain private and unchanged.
# gfx1151 Qwen qualification at TensorFold 1.0.12

Single-GPU model and HTTP equality receipt for [#426](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/426).
Measured on 2026-10-17, on a BOSGAME M5 with an AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`).
The tested source is **`833bbfcba9109bb38c7af7303f80da0ca12b213c`**, tagged `v1.0.12`, with a clean tree.
This receipt does not qualify later `main` commits, other model families, or multi-GPU configurations.
No inference implementation changes are included.

## Environment and checkpoints

- Zig 0.17.0; Ubuntu HIP 7.1.52801-9999; Ubuntu clang 21.1.8.
- The HIP build used `ReleaseFast`, explicit `gfx1151`, and the LLVM 21 device bitcode directory.
- Binary SHA-256 values and the complete build command are in [provenance.json](provenance.json).
- All 48 local checkpoint files checked against public Hugging Face metadata matched their pinned revisions.
  [checkpoints.json](checkpoints.json) retains each Git blob or LFS SHA-256 digest, size and match result.

| Checkpoint | Public repository | Revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-9B, MLX 4-bit | `lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit` | `b455506b0f574c74616dbcd56879bde38fafcff3` |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MLX 4-bit with MTP | `TensorFold/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MLX-4bit-MTP` | `f84b054c5677b6e59bdb969ae61915b0983d68bb` |
| Qwen3.8-27B, MLX 4-bit | `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` | `70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f` |

## Results

| Checkpoint | Model invariants passed | Failed | Skipped | HTTP comparisons exercised and passed | HTTP drafting comparisons not exercised |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 42 | 0 | 5 | 13 | 2 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + MTP | 46 | 0 | 1 | 15 | 0 |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 42 | 0 | 5 | 13 | 2 |
| Total | **130** | **0** | **11** | **41** | **4** |

The unmodified `tf-qwen35-test check` gate exercised row/residual equality, concurrency, graph/eager equality,
resume and radix behavior. Its exact cases and results are retained in `*-model-check.log`.

The unmodified `serve_check.py` exercised solo/concurrent equality, long-prompt interleaving, repeatability,
and its resumed/fresh comparison. It ran under [record-served.py](record-served.py), which wraps `urllib.request.urlopen`
to append each request and response to the `*-serve-check.jsonl` file; for the standard `serve_check.py` run it does not
change request bodies or replies. It also skips the optional extended suites when a `skip-extended` marker exists (below). Greedy and sampled requests use the same public prompts across models.
The HTTP logs retain all fifteen printed `ok` lines per checkpoint, but **45 printed successes do not mean
45 exercised comparisons**: the 9B and 27B have no draft head, so their two drafting comparisons are vacuous.
Those four comparisons are classified as not exercised in the table and [summary.json](summary.json).
The other thirteen HTTP comparisons still execute on those checkpoints.

The 35B requests did draft. In `35b-serve-check.jsonl`, all **36** drafted replies accepted drafts,
**974 of 1593** drafted tokens in all, from each reply's `speculative` telemetry rather than its `draft` flag.
The server log's accepted/drafted counts **30/68, 31/33, 26/46 and 34/51** are the four drafted == serial comparisons.
Both greedy and sampled drafted replies matched plain replies. Drafted == plain covers this one checkpoint only:
the 9B and 27B have no draft head.

The three `*-serve-check.jsonl` files retain all **183 HTTP 200 responses**, their request bodies, complete replies,
cache/speculation telemetry, and native full token SHA-256 values. Independently grouping identical request bodies
while ignoring only `draft` gives **33 groups with zero token-hash mismatches**.
[http-token-hash-audit.json](http-token-hash-audit.json) records that audit separately from the scripts' printed results.

### Skips and remaining coverage

- Eight model drafting controls did not execute: four each on the 9B and 27B, which have no draft head.
- All three model gates skipped `radix memory: too few ids` at the default 1536 synthetic IDs; the control needs 1548.
  It was run afterwards with 2048 IDs and passed on all three checkpoints (see Follow-up below).
- The four unexercised HTTP drafting comparisons above are separate from those eleven model skips.
- Extended `serve_rewind.py` ran on the 9B and was stopped (`rc=-15`); it is incomplete and unqualified, and its partial exchanges are omitted.
  The final requests in `9b-server-8092.log`, ending with one marked `reason=client-left`, are from that stopped run.
  For every later run, `record-served.py` found its `skip-extended` marker and exited 77 before starting `serve_rewind.py`
  or `structured_served.py`, so neither upstream script ran on the 35B or 27B, nor `structured_served.py` on the 9B.
  Neither suite is qualified, and the full structured-output matrix is not covered.
- Refusals: 0 of 183 HTTP requests were rejected (all returned 200). Content refusal behavior was not tested,
  and no deliberate refusal case (for example a prompt past the context window) was sent.
- No independent cross-engine model-accuracy reference, long-context performance comparison,
  multi-GPU run, or other model family is qualified by this receipt. Existing model-free runtime tests were not repeated.
- This is an equality/correctness receipt. Raw timing fields are retained, but no speedup or performance-regression claim is made.

## Reproduction

Use the tested commit and the checkpoint revisions above. Run from that pinned checkout.
`ZIG_DIR` points to the Zig 0.17.0 installation; `MODEL` points to one checkpoint directory.
The same build produced both binaries for all three models:

```sh
"$ZIG_DIR/zig" build native-hip tf-qwen35-test \
  -Dhip-arch=gfx1151 -Dhipcc=/usr/bin/hipcc -Dhip-include=/usr/include \
  -Dhip-device-lib=/usr/lib/llvm-21/lib/clang/21/amdgcn/bitcode \
  -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Dversion=1.0.12 -j4
./zig-out/bin/tf-qwen35-test check "$MODEL"
```

Each model then ran in its own single server process with these flags:

```sh
./zig-out/native-hip/bin/tensorfold-native serve "$MODEL" \
  --backend rocm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8092 --name "$NAME" \
  --context 16384 --parallel 4 --prompt-cache-gib 1 --no-thinking
python3 "$RECEIPT_DIR/record-served.py" zig/tests/qwen35/serve_check.py \
  "$RECEIPT_DIR/$TAG-serve-check.jsonl" http://127.0.0.1:8092 "$NAME" 64
```

`serve_check.py` can also be run directly with the same last three arguments; the recorder only keeps the exchanges.

`NAME` was `amd-9b`, `amd-35b` or `amd-27b`, and `TAG` was `9b`, `35b` or `27b`. Requests use `max_tokens=64`, temperature 0 or 0.8,
seed 7, and `enable_thinking=false`; exact bodies are in the JSONL files.
The initial model gate uses its upstream default synthetic IDs and flags; it does not include the optional truth/accuracy phase.
The successful build was quiet; native execution and the binary hashes identify the executables actually exercised.

## Follow-up: radix memory and cancellation

Run the same day with the same binaries, checkpoints and serve flags.

| Checkpoint | Invariants with 2048 IDs passed | Failed | Skipped | Radix checks passed | `serve_cancel.py` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 43 | 0 | 4 | 8 of 8 | 3 ok, failed 0 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + MTP | 47 | 0 | 0 | 8 of 8 | 3 ok, failed 0 |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 43 | 0 | 4 | 8 of 8 | **failed 3 of 3** |

The remaining skips are the drafting controls of the two checkpoints without a draft head.
[ids2048.npy](ids2048.npy) holds `1000 + (i * 7919) % 50000` for `i < 2048`, the upstream synthetic formula made longer.
`serve_cancel.py` ran with 2,200 prompt words (14,994 tokens), so the long prompt fits the receipt's
16,384-token window; its default 3,000 words (20,438 tokens) are refused before prefill and would test nothing.
Each server log shows the three long requests reaching prefill and ending `reason=client-left` with no tokens,
and no request refused. The script passes when the next short request finishes within 3 s of a solo one:

| Checkpoint | Long request ended, s after it arrived | Next short request | Alone | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 1.66 s | 2.09 s | 0.85 s | pass |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + MTP | 0.79 to 0.84 s | 0.56 to 0.62 s | 0.20 s | pass |
| Qwen3.8-27B | 5.04 to 5.07 s | 6.49 to 6.51 s | 1.90 s | **fail** |

The server's `after=` time counts from when the request arrived; the script drops the connection 0.4 s after sending,
and the time from disconnect to release is not measured separately. On the 27B the cancelled request ended about 5 s
after it arrived, and the next short request waited behind it.
The server prefills in 1024-row chunks; that the cancel waits for the running chunk is our inference, not measured.

```sh
./zig-out/bin/tf-qwen35-test check "$MODEL" --ids ids2048.npy --only invariants
python3 zig/tests/qwen35/serve_cancel.py http://127.0.0.1:8092 "$NAME" 2200
```

# GLM-5.3-Flash FP4-Local on CUDA: final-source receipt

Tested implementation: `80517fc36ea6ee9183c5237ae92b1abd70619f75` (commit.txt has the tree and the eight commits).
Checked after it: `d23862ab`, the three commits above this receipt's first commit (comments and docs, the loader
gate's own checks, the format names and messages; `head-d23862ab/commit.txt`), on their own binaries in
`head-d23862ab/`, and `797dd2e1`, four more (the loader's refusal of an FP8 projection a GPU's lane cannot run,
`readRecipes`' errors, a test of `csfLinear`'s empty-weight refusal and a kernel contract control;
`head-797dd2e1/commit.txt`), on its own binaries in `head-797dd2e1/`. They do not retake the rest of this receipt.
Base: `v1.1.1` (`b10231b94f8adf3d4132acebdc0a1ac87e53a838`); baseline binaries are plain v1.1.1 built the same way (`bin-b10231b9`).
Test date: 2026-10-20. Platform: MSI EdgeXpert (GB10, DGX Spark-compatible; sm_121, 128 GB shared memory), two at
TP=2 over a direct RoCE link (two rails), three at TP=3 over a ring of direct links. Containers pinned to the efficiency
cores (`--cpuset-cpus=0-4,10-14`, as 1.1.1's runbook in #1033).
Toolchain: Zig 0.17.0, nvcc 13.0 (V13.0.88) for sm_121; runtime NCCL 2.30.7. binaries.txt has every binary's sha256.
Checkpoints: `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local` at `76348ddb2be2e35e39ecfc00e75dc07703f4f3d5`,
`nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`.
Grammar: `lib/libtfgrammar.so` from the v1.1.1 release archive (a source build makes no `lib/`); lib/ has its sha256.

## Prepared carry

This full packet is historical contributor evidence. Its results are not rerun qualification of the current main or
this prepared carry. All original files and helper sources are retained; no helper is installed or used by inference.
The independent Python references require their own environment. Current CUDA device gates remain unchecked.
The redaction report accounts for maintainer substitutions; SHA256SUMS covers every packet file except itself.

## Scope

This qualifies FP4-Local loaded as stored and served at TP=2 and TP=3: the loader gate on every layer, the lane
invariants, served exactness (drafted = `"draft": false`, resumed = cold, concurrent = alone, prompts admitted together
= alone), media and video, structured output and tool calls, prompt logprobs against a BF16 reference, per-rank load and
peak memory, the kernel contract and glm-ref, the no-GPU CI steps, NVFP4 before and after against plain v1.1.1, and
FP4-Local against NVFP4 on matched inputs. It does not qualify Metal, or a comparison with vLLM.

## Reproduction

Every serve: `tensorfold-native serve CKPT --name local-model --parallel 4 --context 40960 --port 8095`, drafts on, one
rank a host (`TF_GLM_RANK`, `TF_GLM_WORLD`), each host's page cache of both checkpoints dropped first; `md*` and `mr-*`
add `--vision`, `vd-*` and `vl-*` add `--vision` with the library in the server's `../lib` (`vl-*` with
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` naming it), `x9-*-nd` add `--no-drafts`, and `bt-*` set `TF_GLM_PROMPT_STEPS=0`. The checks are
tools/: `golden_http.py` on dc.json, upstream's `bench_concurrent.py`, `bench_openai.py` and `bench_cache.py`,
`openai_aligned.py` (the `"draft": false` decode), `resume_http.py`, `batch_http.py` (`one-pass` for `bt-*`),
`media_http.py`, `media_resume_http.py`, `video_http.py` (`video_served.py`'s 15 checks over HTTP and a repeat, against
the ids `video_ref.py` takes from transformers 5.19.0 and PyAV 19.0.1 on clips `glm_video_fixtures.py` makes;
`video/clips-sha256.txt`), `x9_live.py` (and its `compare`), `s5_prompt_lp.py` (prompt_logprobs 20 on the 128 held-out
sequences) with `s5_compare.py` against `s5_bf16_ref.py`'s reference. `mkprompts.py` makes the matched token-id files.
runs.log has one line a check.

## Remaining coverage limits

- TP=3 needs `TF_GLM_MM=0` on every rank: the default glm_mm refuses KDA's input stack there with `BadShape`
  (#1067, whose thread has plain 1.1.1's run; here `tp3/serve/smoke3-mm1`, this branch with the bootstrap on FP4-Local),
  so TP=3 has no batched prompt pass (it needs glm_mm's tiles).
- TP=3's ranks meet through a local bootstrap commit that is not part of this branch (`tp3/bootstrap.patch`); the
  gate and the lanes at TP=3 ran this branch's own binaries.
- 1.1.1's batched prompt pass runs only with `TF_GLM_PROMPT_STEPS=0` on rank 0; `bt-*` set it, the other serves ran
  the default.
- `797dd2e1`'s refusal at load of an FP8 projection the lane cannot run applies on a GPU without thread block
  clusters (before sm_90); every GPU here is a GB10, where every FP8 lane weight fits, so it was not run.
- The KL is over BF16's top 20 only, and both sides' logits are bf16, so best tokens tie; `s5-compare.json` also
  gives top-1 equal within ties.
- runs.log's FAIL lines: `smoke3-mm1` is the #1067 probe above; the first `x9-fl` ran before `libtfgrammar.so` was in
  place (HTTP 400 naming it) and its retake is the one published; `single` is the limits line above, on this head, on
  `797dd2e1` and on plain v1.1.1 alike; `vd-fl`, `vd-nv` and `vd-111` are the refused video serves (#1107). The tamper
  controls in `head-d23862ab/gate-controls/` print FAIL for the flipped upload and its rank before their PASS line: the
  control passes when that is all that fails.
- Metal and MLX were not run (no Mac). No vLLM comparison is claimed.

## Publication handling

Machine names, internal addresses, home paths, working-session names, and the tools' local document, records, container and image names replaced, CRLF line ends made LF and trailing blanks dropped; result
values, token ids and token hashes kept.
`redaction-report.json` counts the replacements a file. The memory wrapper's receipts are raw for TP=2 `ex-fl` only;
`memory/summary.json` summarizes every receipt with its original's sha256. The prompt-logprob rows (87 MB a
checkpoint) are not included; `s5/plp-sha256.txt` has their sha256. SHA256SUMS pins every published file except
itself.
# GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA: KV pages from the core pool, receipt

Tested implementation: the binaries built from `0b094b74…`, commit 11 of #1163 (commit.txt has the tree and the
commits): commits 1 to 7 are the change, 8 to 10 add the kernel contract's tests, gate 5's records and two host tests,
and 11 fixes a bug the first TP=3 run found (below). After it, `cbe29802` puts a comment on one line and this
receipt's commit adds this folder: neither changes engine or kernel source. The kernel contract ran on `3b41fd7c`
(commit 10); commit 11 changes no kernel. TP=3's ranks ran commit 11's engine source with two local commits for the
ring, which are not part of #1163 (`tp3/ring.patch`): rank 0's NCCL id handed to the other ranks in a file, so that a
ring of /32 links bootstraps (#1178 is the upstream way), and a heat ceiling (`TF_HEAT_CEILING`: a prompt chunk also
waits while its expected rise would pass the ceiling), which changes when chunks run, not what they compute.
Base: main `f8d254c5…` (after 1.1.2); main's binary for the replay and the speed A/B was built the same way
(`bin-f8d254c5`).
Test dates: 2026-10-22 and 10-23. Platform: MSI EdgeXpert (GB10, DGX Spark-compatible; sm_121, 128 GB shared
memory), two at TP=2 over a direct RoCE link, three at TP=3 over a ring of direct links; driver 580.178.04. Ranks in
Ubuntu 24.04 containers pinned to the efficiency cores (`--cpuset-cpus=0-4,10-14`), NCCL 2.30.7.
Toolchain: Zig 0.17.0, nvcc 13.3 (V13.3.73) for sm_121; gate 5's records also with nvcc 13.0 (V13.0.88), both for
sm_80, 86, 89, 120 and 121. binaries.txt has every binary's sha256.
Checkpoint: `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`.

## Scope

This qualifies GLM's streams on KV pages from the core pool at TP=2 and TP=3: the paged streams against their
whole-window twins byte for byte, the ranks' agreement on one pool, served exactness on pages (concurrent = alone,
drafted = `"draft": false`, resumed = fresh, images), the replies against main's, a long prompt beside short ones,
admission when the pool is short and when more requests arrive at once than there are paged sequences, speed against
main at TP=2, the kernel contract with gate 5's records, the no-GPU CI and the mutations. It does not qualify FP8
caches on pages (refused by name), DFlash2 drafts (no weights here), Metal or MLX.

## The bug commit 11 fixes

The first TP=3 run, on `b7fecb3d` (`tp3/found-b7fecb3d/r6all/`), served `TF_KV_PAGES=all` at `--parallel 8`. With
`all` the engine's own sequence stays idle, so eight lanes have seven paged sequences. Eight requests that arrive
together are admitted before any of them opens (the pool's check then sees every paged sequence free), and the last to
open took slot 8: binding it made a whole-window sequence, 12.88 GiB at a 1M window, before the pages refused it with
`LaneMemory`. Rank 0's host fell from 11 GiB free to 4 GiB in two seconds, its memory guard stopped the server
(`hostwatch-rank0.log`, `KILLED`), the other ranks ended on the closed line, and 53 of the 60 alone comparisons and 40
of the 72 `"draft": false` ones failed; none was unequal. TP=2's `all` (`--parallel 4`, a 128k window) took the same
path and made 1.77 GiB for slot 4, inside its reserve, so its replies were all equal. Commit 11 takes a stream's pages
before its sequence is bound: a slot past the paged sequences waits for one and nothing is made for it. Every served
run in this folder but that one ran commit 11.

## Reproduction

Every serve: `tensorfold-native serve CKPT --name glm-tf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8097 --max-tokens 32768
--reasoning-effort high --parallel P --context C`, drafts on, one rank a host (`TF_GLM_RANK`, `TF_GLM_WORLD`),
`TF_HEAT_HIGH=92 TF_HEAT_LOW=88 TF_HEAT_CEILING=93`. TP=2: `--context 131072 --parallel 4`; `r2all`, `r2on` and
`r2vis` add `--prompt-cache-gib 4` and `TF_KV_POISON=1` with `TF_KV_PAGES` `all` or `on`, `r2vis` `--vision`;
`r2auto` and `r2main` and every speed serve `--prompt-cache-gib 0`. TP=3: `--context 1048576 --parallel 8` and
`TF_KV_POISON=1`; `r6auto` with `TF_KV_PAGES` unset and the default prompt cache (16 GiB), `r6all` `TF_KV_PAGES=all`,
`r6admit` `TF_KV_PAGES=all` with a 22.8 GiB prompt cache (the `all` serve's room less its streams' fixed parts and 0.9 GiB), `r6off`
`TF_KV_PAGES=off --prompt-cache-gib 0 --parallel auto`; NCCL over the ring's direct links with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, and
each TP=3 host's memory guard (v3's `hostwatch.sh`: the server stopped below 5 GiB free). The checks are the
repository's tools: `bench_concurrent.py --alone --serial --tokens 256 --reps 1`, `reuse_served.py` (`record --planned
--min-prompt 2048`, `replay`, `compare`, `cold`, `ids`), `bench_openai.py`, `bench_cache.py --require-cold`; here
`media_http.py`, `media_resume_http.py`, `kvp_admit.py` and `kvp_sum.py` (tools/; `kvp_sum.py conc` ends non-zero
when a request failed or a reply differed). `tf-cuda-test glm-paged-check CKPT RANK WORLD IDFILE` with
`TF_GLM_LAYERS=5`. runs/ has the chains' own output.

## Remaining coverage limits

- TP=3's ranks ran commit 11's engine source with `tp3/ring.patch` (above); TP=2's and one GPU's ran commit 11 alone.
- Ranks 1 and 2 of the TP=3 check print their PASS lines in the middle of NCCL's INFO lines (`NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`).
- Speed against main was measured at TP=2 only; TP=3's cold prompt times are in `tp3/serve/r6auto/cold.json`, with no
  main serve beside them.
- `--kv-cache fp8` keeps windows: `auto` does not page and `on` and `all` are refused (`Fp8OnPages`).
- DFlash2 (`--drafter`): no weights here; the drafts on pages are the MTP head's.
- Metal and MLX were not run (no Mac).

## Publication handling

CRLF line ends made LF, trailing blanks dropped and an indent with a space before a tab made spaces (as `git diff
--check` asks; four lines of two mutations' stack traces); machine names, internal addresses, home and local paths, and the
work's session, plan, records, container and image names replaced with placeholders (`redaction-report.json` counts
them a file; host-a to host-c run TP=3's ranks 0 to 2, host-d and host-e TP=2's ranks 0 and 1); result values, token
ids and token hashes kept. The TP=3 server logs keep NCCL's INFO lines as they were written. The reuse records keep
their rows without the request bodies (3 MB a record): each row has its body's sha256 and size, and
`records-sha256.txt` the originals'. The speed runs' prompt files are not included: `reuse_served.py cold` and `ids`
make them again. SHA256SUMS pins every published file except itself.

A maintainer pass also replaces residual numbered host references, two interleaved host fragments and a local synthetic-checkpoint directory with role placeholders. The additional counts are in `redaction-report.json`; numerical results, token ids and token hashes are unchanged.

Archived helper docstrings are normalized to one line for publication; their executable AST and CLI behavior are unchanged.
# GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA: the engine's own sequence on KV pages, receipt

Tested implementation: the binaries built from `8e705835…`, commit 20: #1163's 14 commits and the first six of the
pull request that stacks on it (commit.txt has the tree and the commits). The receipt's commit adds this folder and
changes no source. TP=3's ranks ran commit 20's engine source with the two local commits for the ring that #1163's
receipt describes (`tp3/ring.patch`): rank 0's NCCL id handed to the other ranks in a file (#1178 is the upstream
way), and a heat ceiling (`TF_HEAT_CEILING`: a prompt chunk also waits while its expected rise would pass the
ceiling), which changes when chunks run, not what they compute.
Base: #1163's head `d7ff6494…`, on main `f8d254c5…` (after 1.1.2); main's binary for the replay and the speed A/B
was built the same way (`bin-f8d254c5`).
Test date: 2026-10-23. Platform: MSI EdgeXpert (GB10, DGX Spark-compatible; sm_121, 128 GB shared memory), two at
TP=2 over a direct RoCE link, three at TP=3 over a ring of direct links; driver 580.178.04. Ranks in Ubuntu 24.04
containers pinned to the efficiency cores (`--cpuset-cpus=0-4,10-14`), NCCL 2.30.7.
Toolchain: Zig 0.17.0, nvcc 13.3 (V13.3.73) for sm_121. binaries.txt has every binary's sha256.
Checkpoint: `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`.

## Scope

This qualifies the engine's own sequence (slot 0) on KV pages at TP=2 and TP=3: slot 0 on pages from its init
against its whole-window twin byte for byte, the ranks' agreement on `TF_KV_PAGES`, served exactness with every
stream on pages (concurrent = alone, drafted = `"draft": false`, resumed = fresh, images), the replies against main's,
the floor (one window of pages planned before the rest) holding a long request while short ones share the pool,
admission when the pool is down to its floor, speed against main at TP=2, the no-GPU CI and the mutations. The
kernels are #1163's, unchanged, so the kernel contract and gate 5's records are in #1163's receipt. It does not
qualify FP8 caches on pages (refused by name, as in #1163), DFlash2 drafts (no weights here), Metal or MLX.

## What changed for these runs

- `TF_KV_PAGES=all` is now `on`: every stream, the engine's own among them, is on pages. So `r2all` and `r2on` serve
  the same configuration twice, and `r6all` is the concurrency check at a 96k window with all eight streams on pages.
- Every rank resolves `TF_KV_PAGES` and the ranks agree on it; the chains pass the same environment to every rank.
- The floor is shown two ways: `r6admit` serves a 96k window with the pool down to its floor and a page a stream
  (64k requests: one fits, the next waits), and `r6auto` serves seven 2k prompts beside a 64k conversation at a 1M
  window. No request was sent at 1M tokens (below).

- No request reached a 1M-token window's length: the floor's pages for one such request are in each 1M startup line
  ("enough for one at a 1048576-token window"), and `r6admit` shows the floor holding a 64k request at a 96k window.
- TP=3's ranks ran commit 20's engine source with `tp3/ring.patch` (above); TP=2's and one GPU's ran commit 20 alone.
- Ranks 1 and 2 of the TP=3 check print their PASS lines in the middle of NCCL's INFO lines (`NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`).
- Speed against main was measured at TP=2 only.
- `--kv-cache fp8` keeps windows: `auto` does not page and `on` and `all` are refused (`Fp8OnPages`).
- DFlash2 (`--drafter`): no weights here; the drafts on pages are the MTP head's.
- Metal and MLX were not run (no Mac).

# HIP refuses an external drafter (gfx1151)

Receipts for [#1044](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/1044). On the HIP engine, `serve --drafter` and
`tensorfold benchmark --drafter` each stop with one diagnostic before any weights load. Refusing the external
DFlash2 drafter does not turn drafting off: the engine's own drafts stay on.

Measured on 2026-10-18 from 17:33 to 17:42 UTC (19:33 to 19:42 CEST) on one Bosgame M5: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395,
Radeon 8060S (`gfx1151`), Linux. The checkpoint is `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit` at
`70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f`, read offline from the Hugging Face cache (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`,
`run-script.sh` line 50). `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` was in the same cache: serve resolves `--drafter` to its
folder before the engine opens, and that lookup succeeded, since the serve refusal below comes from the engine.

The source was a local merge on the box, `7b84f909`, never pushed: `main` at `76aafcf2` with #1043 at `5906a3f7`,
this PR at `920d1348` and #1045 at `1b4b2d7b`. This PR's runtime code at `920d1348` is the code at its head; later
commits change comments, one test name, docs and these receipts only. The binary was built by
`zig build native-hip -Dhip-arch=gfx1151 ... -Doptimize=ReleaseFast` with Zig 0.17.0 (`run-script.sh` line 46,
`build_exit=0` at `run.log` line 38, an empty `build.log`). Its SHA-256, as recorded on the box (`run.log` line 39):
`e279e29a54b56dc81ff70985f8c4cffaa0d9aff4a7456a234eb7247667492247`. The `Draft counts` line and
`27b-auto.drafts.json` come from #1045, not from this PR.

## The refusals: one diagnostic each, before any weights load

Below, `$B` is that binary and `$M27` is `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit`, as in `run-script.sh`. Each refusal's
log is the command's whole output (stdout and stderr) and is one line long: the diagnostic is printed once, and
nothing is printed before or after it.

| Run | Command (`run-script.sh`) | Exit (`run.log`) | The whole log |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| R2a | line 54: `$B benchmark $M27 --drafter z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 --output .../27b-dflash2.json` | 1 (line 43) | `27b-dflash2.log` line 1 |
| R2b | line 55: `timeout 180 $B serve $M27 --backend rocm --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8093 --drafter z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` | 1 (line 46) | `27b-serve-drafter.log` line 1 |

`27b-dflash2.log` line 1:
`tensorfold benchmark: --drafter: the HIP engine runs no DFlash2 drafter yet, so a rocm run takes none; --drafter none runs without it`

`27b-serve-drafter.log` line 1:
`tensorfold: --drafter: the HIP engine runs no DFlash2 drafter yet; serve without --drafter`

**R2a stops before the run starts.** A run's first output is its suite banner, as in `27b-auto.log` lines 1 and 2
(`community-v1: ...` and `This generates model replies; ...`). R2a's log has neither. No receipt was written
(`run.log` line 44: `ls: cannot access '~/tf-1001-runs/out/27b-dflash2.json'`). In the code the refusal is the
first check once the checkpoint's family is known, before the drafter cache lookup and before any serve child
(`zig/src/server/benchmark.zig` line 338, `if (rocm and given) return fail(ctx, rocm_drafter);`; the banner is
lines 381-382).

**R2b stops before any weights load.** The refusal is the first line of `checkGroup` (`zig/src/native/hip.zig`
line 54). `ready()` runs `checkGroup` first (line 84), before it reads the model's window, queries the GPU (line 92)
or prints the policy (line 102), and `openWith` runs `ready()` (line 218) before the family's `open` reads any
weights (line 224). A follower rank goes through `ready()` too (line 252). A HIP serve that gets past that point
prints three lines on its way to serving: the policy line `[tensorfold] HIP rank 0 of 1: policy ...`, the device
line naming the model's size, and `serving ... loaded in N s`. For this checkpoint on a Bosgame M5 they are
lines 2, 4 and 5 of `docs/receipts/gfx1151-qwen-833bbfcb/27b-server-8092.log` (`model 14.10 GiB`,
`loaded in 37.9s`). R2b's log has none of them.

**Both finished within one second.** `run-script.sh` prints a GPU reading (`gtt()`, line 12, stamped with
`date -u +%T`) after R1, before R2b and after R2b. All three are stamped `17:42:02` (`run.log` lines 42, 45
and 47), so R2a and R2b each started and exited within that second, against the 37.9 s this checkpoint took to
load in that earlier receipt. R2b exited 1 by itself, not 124 from `timeout`. The GTT readings (1,129,906,176
then 1,129,861,120 bytes) are taken outside the process, after it exited: they show nothing was left held, not
that nothing was allocated.
The evidence for "before any weights load" is the one-line logs, the timing and the code path above.

These runs are one rank on one GPU. The refusal on a follower rank (`--tp 2 --rank 1`) is covered by the host
test in `zig/src/native/hip.zig`, not by a GPU run.

## What still drafts: refusing DFlash2 does not mean plain decoding

R1 is `$B benchmark $M27 --output .../27b-auto.json` (`run-script.sh` line 52), with the default `--drafter auto`.
It ran from 17:33:19 to 17:42:02 (`run.log` lines 40 to 42) and exited 0. `27b-auto.log` line 3 says
`This run passes no drafter: the HIP engine runs no DFlash2 drafter yet.`, the receipt `27b-auto.json` has
`"drafter_repo_id": null`, and `27b-auto.drafts.json` has `"drafter_passed": false`.

The run still drafted. Its 20 attempts drafted 262 tokens and kept 70 of them, over 5,030 rounds
(`27b-auto.drafts.json` `totals`, and `27b-auto.log` line 37). These drafts did not come from an MTP head,
because this checkpoint has none. At this revision `model.safetensors.index.json` (git blob `05a3a3a1`, the digest
pinned in `docs/receipts/gfx1151-qwen-833bbfcb/checkpoints.json`) lists 2,180 tensors and none of them is an
`mtp` tensor, and the revision has no `mtp*.safetensors` file. The HIP engine looks for a head in
`mtp*.safetensors` or among the shards' own tensors, and the shards hold the same 2,180 (`Checkpoint.mtp` in
`zig/src/families/qwen3_5/weights/checkpoint.zig`), and the 1.0.12 model check on this checkpoint reports `the
model has no draft head` (`docs/receipts/gfx1151-qwen-833bbfcb/27b-model-check.log` line 29). The policy line's
`mtp drafts 3 under 0.3` is the policy, printed whether or not a head loads. An earlier reading in the PR
description took these drafts for MTP drafts; they are not.

What drafted is the lane core's copy proposer (`SuffixLookup`): it proposes tokens copied from the stream's own
context, on every request that drafts. The counts fit it: 6 of the 20 attempts drafted nothing in about 255
rounds, and the others drafted 15, 34 or 48 tokens each. An MTP head proposes on most rounds: the MTP checkpoint
in `docs/receipts/gfx1151-qwen-833bbfcb/35b-server-8092.log` shows `rounds=33 accepted=30/68`, for example.
On a checkpoint with MTP weights the HIP engine drafts with the head as well as with copies. `serve --mtp-drafts 0`
stops the head's drafts alone (the head still loads); `serve --no-drafts`, or `tensorfold benchmark --serial`,
turns both off and decodes plain.

## Numerical evidence

`projection-fp64-bounds.json` covers 66 projection/layout cells and 60,954,624 outputs.
The actual shared FP32 helper was captured before BF16 storage and compared with independently unpacked affine FP64 products.
No raw FP32 or BF16-store error exceeded the existing derived bounds. Worst-column errors were retained.

The row-pair optimization invokes the same shared helper and preserves its accumulation order.
All 132 checkpoint comparisons at widths 1 and 64 produced 123,814,080 bytes identical to the old selector.
A separate 8,193-token before/after check compared all 2,097,408,000 BF16 logit bytes exactly.
Thus this optimization does not worsen any output-based precision metric on those comparisons.

`fidelity-investigation.json` records the first actual primitive difference and its causal propagation.
Official MLX 0.32.4 uses different effective affine reconstruction in its vector and matrix paths.
The native engine consistently follows the FP32 affine equation rather than changing arithmetic with batch width.
The first captured FP32 error was about 6.81e-9, inside the existing derived 5.52e-5 pre-store bound;
it crossed a BF16 midpoint and propagated through recurrent history.

`model-fp64-comparison.json` retains all 18 originally disjoint native/MLX positions, including repeated histories.
With direct binary64-to-BF16 rounding, native belongs to the ideal model maximum set in nine cases, MLX in 16,
both in eight and neither in one. This ideal FP64 model is a diagnostic; it does not execute the native FP32 reductions.
No new tie tolerance or end-to-end acceptance threshold was applied. The primitive evidence does not replace that model gate.

The oracle is reproducible with `tools/lfm3/fp64_reference.py`; its tests include all finite BF16 encodings,
adjacent midpoints, double rounding, subnormals, overflow and six-bit cross-word unpacking.

## Binned projection candidate

`binned-projection.json` records the explicit candidate at `75478ed17`; ordinary model loading leaves it disabled.
It preserves each input value while partitioning exponent ranges and exact code nibbles. M5 uses the shared
`nax.h` tensor-unit fragments; M4 uses its fallback. Group affine sums use compensated FP32 pairs.
The integer argument is limited to finite normal aligned products without overflow or underflow.
It does not establish universal FP64 equivalence for extreme BF16 subnormals or arbitrary inputs.

The actual native M5 tool produced **61,907,040/61,907,040** direct FP64-to-BF16 reference values across 132 captures:
11 projection classes, all six checkpoints, and prompt/decode widths 64 and 1. All 66 first-row comparisons matched.
The six small attention-gate cells use the unchanged row fallback and are included explicitly.
No column had more FP64 error than either the retained original-native or MLX result.
Those two comparator captures are from the M4, not a same-device M5 performance comparison.
The file retains worst-column metrics, input/output hashes, artifact identities and the complete contract summaries.
Both M4 and M5 passed all six operator variants, both planted controls and launch limits.
These primitive results do not settle whole-model fidelity or served performance.

To reconstruct the fixtures, save `fixture_tokens` as a little-endian uint32 NPY array and run the default
`tf-lfm3-forward MODEL TOKENS.npy baseline.bf16 trace TRACE_DIR` for each named checkpoint.
Concatenate the trace files ending in `_<input_stage>.bf16` in filename order to recreate each `input_file`;
the first `2*k` bytes recreate its `one_row_file`. Verify the recorded input hash before comparing outputs.
Run `tf-lfm3-project MODEL MODULE INPUT.bf16 ROWS OUTPUT.bf16 --binned` at widths 64 and 1.
Save the receipt’s `cases` array as `manifest.json` beside the inputs for `tools/lfm3/projection_compare.py`.
Use the frozen candidate commit for these artifact identities.

`binned-row-twin.json` records the later opt-in row twin at `5a2bdea76`: all 132 captures retain
123,814,080 bytes exactly against the earlier FP64-exact tiled captures. Both M4 and M5 pass six
variants and two planted controls. The twin remains disabled for ordinary model loading because
its serving performance has not passed; these operator results do not qualify a whole model.

## Controlled performance

`cold-prefill-ab.json` contains all 16 matched pairs / 32 fresh-server cold requests.
It includes full output-token hashes, body hashes, client TTFT, engine prefill time and peak physical process footprint.
Both sides used the same body, exact prompt counts, 16 output tokens, context 70,000, four configured lanes and zero cached tokens.
The 2k and 8k cells have three alternating pairs each; 32k and 64k have one pair each.
Only 4-bit performance was measured.

Engine prefill seconds, before to after:

- Text: 2k 1.239530 to 0.812959; 8k 5.307524 to 3.608895; 32k 27.314691 to 20.488389; 64k 73.402432 to 61.632933.
- VL decoder, text requests: 2k 1.261845 to 0.815432; 8k 5.402433 to 3.617449; 32k 27.686643 to 20.536702; 64k 73.920498 to 59.646930.

These are engine prefill times, not client TTFT. All 16 paired full output-token hashes matched.
At 64k, physical footprint was 2,926,167,768 to 2,925,315,776 bytes for text and
3,586,115,720 to 3,584,559,264 bytes for VL. Device/pinned allocator peaks were not collected.

`decode-concurrency.json` records 256-token, three-repetition code/prose runs.
All 60 concurrent-to-solo comparisons and all eight serial checks matched.
Small decode-rate differences are descriptive; they are not a separately established speedup.

Earlier standard-server comparisons still showed MLX-VLM faster, especially for long cold prefill.
[`m5-text-slice-vs-mlx.json`](m5-text-slice-vs-mlx.json) measures this slice alone against mlx-vlm at all three widths:
cold prefill is about a tenth of its rate. The stacked LFM3-VL PR carries the prompt and attention speed work.
The faster arithmetic-changing matrix candidate failed the strict no-worse precision comparison and was excluded.
The slower uniform-exponential candidate was also excluded. No unvalidated GQA experiment is enabled.

## Paired FFN and CPU greedy follow-up

`greedy-dual.json` records the subsequent immutable `b804c6ed` native build.
The FFN gate/up projections share one dispatch while retaining each projection's shared helper and BF16 stores.
A SIMD CPU greedy reduction preserves the first maximum, signed-zero ties and nonfinite rejection;
masked and positive-temperature sampling keep the original path.
All 58 LFM3 kernel checks passed, all 16 controls were red, and launch limits had zero problems.

## Reproduce

Use the pinned Zig version and a complete local checkpoint. Developer references need NumPy; the MLX reference also needs MLX.

```sh
zig build native tf-lfm3-forward tf-lfm3-project tf-lfm3-profile tf-lfm3-exact tf-kernel-contract -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig build test test-lfm3-host test-kernel-contract test-golden fuzz-cortheon -Dcpu=apple_m1

python3 tools/lfm3/reference.py --model-dir MODEL_DIR --tokens TOKENS.npy --output mlx.bf16

./zig-out/bin/tf-lfm3-forward MODEL_DIR TOKENS.npy native.bf16
./zig-out/bin/tf-lfm3-profile MODEL_DIR TOKENS.npy profile.json
```

Repeat the served command for all six checkpoints. Run one model process per GPU, using the native lock and admission guards.
The synthetic cold-prompt request bodies and rendered token arrays are regenerated by `tools/lfm3/cold_prompts.py` (`--write DIR`); it checks all 16 files against the SHA-256 hashes in `cold-prompt-sha256.json`.
The native server did not return its rendered arrays, so matching counts are not described as a captured native-token identity proof.
To repeat cold HTTP measurements, start a fresh owned server with `--context 70000 --parallel 4 --prompt-cache-gib 0`,
POST a saved body to `/v1/chat/completions`, and retain usage, full token hash and timings from the stream.
The supplied bodies omit the optional model alias. Keep the exact bodies unchanged between compared builds.

The explicit decode mode prefills the first 63 rows of this fixture, then executes the last token with one row.

Slice the matching final FP64 row before comparing; do not label a row from a 32-row native block as decode:

```sh

```

`six-width-fp64-prompt.json` reports all 64 prompt rows for both families at 4/6/8 bits.
`six-width-fp64-decode.json` reports the actual one-row decode for those six checkpoints.
`all-fp64-top-differences.json` reports every native/FP64 top difference in the 17 previously selected prompt cells,
with both margins, cross-contender gaps and the worst rows and columns. It does not select only the original 18 MLX disagreements.
The prompt receipts identify the earlier post-RoPE diagnostic binary; they are not final prompt-tile qualification.

To determine whether a discrepancy follows from production reduction rounding, replay the independent affine calculation:

```sh
python3 tools/lfm3/fp64_reference.py --model-dir MODEL_DIR --tokens TOKENS.npy --output rounded.bf16 --projection-rounding metal-row
python3 tools/lfm3/compare_logits.py --native native-prompt.bf16 --reference rounded.bf16 --tokens TOKENS.npy --vocabulary 128000 --phase prompt --output rounded.json
```

This option changes the affine projection reduction only. Remaining operations retain the FP64 reference arithmetic.
`row_projection_reference.py` independently unpacks the checkpoint, rounds each lane's operations to FP32,
then applies the reduction tree. It does not cast the final FP64 model output to manufacture agreement.
The fused affine step uses an FP64 multiply-add followed by FP32 rounding; the recorded checkpoint replay is not a general IEEE fmaf proof.
`projection-rounding-replay.json` records exact equality of all 1,579,008 captured pre-store FP32 outputs for the first VL4 projection.
No end-to-end tolerance or automatic fidelity pass is applied by these tools.

For image-conditioned text, pass independently computed projected rows as a numeric two-dimensional NumPy array:

```sh
python3 tools/lfm3/fp64_reference.py --model-dir MODEL_DIR --tokens TOKENS.npy --image-rows projected.npy --image-start START --output fp64-image-text.bf16
```

The reference validates the entire image-placeholder span, geometry and finite values, then inserts the rounded projected rows.
Supplying native projected rows isolates the decoder; supplying FP64 projected rows additionally measures vision propagation.
These two experiments must be named separately. The input option itself does not qualify a real-image vision fixture.

The optional CPU accelerator has no native inference or build dependency. Compile and select it explicitly:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O3 -ffp-contract=off -shared -fPIC tools/lfm3/row_projection_replay.c -o row-replay.so
LFM3_ROW_REPLAY_LIBRARY="$PWD/row-replay.so" python3 tools/lfm3/fp64_reference.py --model-dir MODEL_DIR --tokens TOKENS.npy --output rounded.bf16 --projection-rounding metal-row
```

Only the explicit affine `fmaf` contracts operations. Input sums and placed inputs are prepared once without changing their order.
Both implementations reproduce all 1,579,008 recorded pre-store FP32 values exactly; integer fixtures exercise all three bit widths.
`rounding-reproduction.json` retains the original ideal-FP64 contenders and the rounded reference's maximum sets and margins.

`real-image-fp64.json` pins the official model card's cat URL, downloaded JPEG, canonical PNG and patch hashes.
The photographed image produces 70 projected rows. It reports all vision-row errors and separates identical-input decoder comparisons
from native/FP64 towers feeding their own rows. On identical FP64 projected rows, the 6/8-bit decoders match all 16 suffix top tokens;
the 4-bit decoder has one lowest-index difference with overlapping maximum sets. With each tower feeding its own rows, 4/6-bit match
all 16 suffix top tokens; 8-bit matches 14/16. Those different-input results are retained and are not an accepted end-to-end pass.
This is one real-image fixture, not a broad real-image benchmark.

The download URL can change its bytes; reproduce this receipt only with the recorded hashes.
The image itself is not redistributed here. The token fixture is the `tokens` array in `real-image-fp64.json`:


# PR 1381 standalone review fixes

## Composition with requested main `cb036e00f`

The shared-reservation stack is integrated without restoring the rejected shared-round guard.
Historical grants and new reservations remain distinct:

1. `granted_depth` reads the last **verified** grant, its short-grant flag and configured slack. Its periodic
   zero-grant probe is evaluated once. This bounds what the next reservation may request.
2. The shared allocator reserves rows using the drafter's cached chain chances, even when that historical
   depth bound exists. The reservation decision queries a stateful copy proposer once.
3. The actual reservation is capped to the hold pass's padded capacity, then `payHolds` prices only its
   positive holds. Expected gain is recomputed from the usable chance prefix. These steps only reduce depths.
4. A fresh zero reservation therefore never offers a hold. A historical zero grant may still probe, but only
   if the new reservation supplies positive rows. Context absorption continues before the depth-zero skip,
   so later holds retain continuous history.

`limit_shared_drafts` keeps upstream's legacy head-step-cost meaning. LFM2's target facts set it, but upstream's
attached-drafter classification excludes its legacy cap for node prices and confidence floors. The opt-in
`granted_depth` path composes its own bound with reservations independently; it neither reinterprets
`Stream.granted` nor replaces the drafter's chain chances with generic rates. Confidence and other-family
legacy caps retain their existing paths.

The focused regressions cover bounds, zero-to-positive transitions, chance pricing, padded-pass capacity,
reserved gain, probe cadence and copy lookup. The mechanical merge without the composition fails seven of
the nine new regressions. An independently compiled host API smoke also reproduces an unpaid hold pass
before the fix: four positive holds survive a 1000 ms hold price. With the composition they are all rejected;
profitable holds remain and zero reservations stay zero, without mutating historical grant fields.

Current-main scoped checks use Zig 0.17.0 and `-Dcpu=apple_m1 -Dversion=1.2.0`:

```sh
zig build native test-native test-shared-lane-regressions-host \
  test-shared-head-cost-metal-host test-draft-metal-host test-contract-images-host \
  -Dcpu=apple_m1 -Dversion=1.2.0 -j2
```

The lane suite passes 299/299, including the complete absorbed-history comparison before every later hold;
the Metal family head-cost checks pass 48/48, draft-host checks 11/11, and native checks 93 with three skips.
The pinned main checker (`985356b424269b8d11e8a486223cf3c9aa1e726bb4761ad4a414482352024367`)
reports 424 inherited findings on both trees, zero new. Only obsolete comparisons against deliberately wasted
holds/full-block counts were removed: reservations now optimize both sides of those comparisons. Token
equality, copy-skip, bound, price and zero-row gates remain.

The historical results below retain their original source and device scope. They do not qualify the new
DSpark chain's complete no-slowdown matrix.

## Historical device receipt

Main's normal suffix copying remains enabled. The integration also checks explicit `draft:false` oracles.

Hold retention is measured on a separate diagnostic build: count positive stream budgets entering and leaving `payHolds`, after the one-pass cap. Report both kept/offered and kept/sum-of-stream-budget-opportunities. The latter includes zero-budget slots in calls that reach this pricing path; it does not count rounds that never call this path. Zero-budget streams do not enter its denominator, probes follow normal pricing, and tail rounds can have fewer live streams than the request batch. Per-call events are retained. Diagnostic output is excluded from throughput runs.

To reproduce, use `device_report.py` with Python's standard library and the `qualification.py` helper from PR 1394's receipts. The driver uses `/tmp/tensorfold-model.lock`, refuses an existing recognized model process through the helper, and aborts on memory-pressure admission changes. Reserve the GPU exclusively. The diagnostic build adds only before/after positive-budget counters around `payHolds`; the executed instrumentation is retained in the receipt.

No new M1/M2/M3/M4, CUDA or HIP device qualification is claimed. Cold-prefill scaling, long-context and cancellation were not rerun for this standalone review report; historical PR 1394 checks are separately scoped to their recorded sources.

## Tools

- `tools/ab.py` (Nemotron) and `tools/abn.py` (Gemma 4, which has no logprobs on CUDA): one arm. Drops the page cache,
  starts a server, sends one warm-up, then three cold prompts each at 2K, 16K and 32K (synthetic word lists, seeded),
  16 tokens at temperature 0. Then decode (128 tokens), one seeded sampled reply, Nemotron's prompt_logprobs, and two
  prompt-cache turns on a second server. TTFT is read from the server's own `done` line.
- `tools/gate.py` (Nemotron) and `tools/gaten.py` (Gemma 4): the comparison. Arms in the order base, new, new, base.
  TTFT change = median of the six new prompts over the median of the six base prompts, per length; content (reply,
  token sha, logprobs, prompt_logprobs, seeded, kept turns) must be equal in every arm; the range per length was set
  before each run.
- `tools/ab2k.py` and `tools/gate2k.py`: Nemotron at 2K, 12 prompts an arm, level = median change <= +0.5 %.
- `tools/abba.py`: the base, new, new, base driver (the runs used an equivalent shell loop), e.g.
  `abba.py ab.py BASE_BIN NEW_BIN MODEL OUT gate.py -0.7 0.7 -2.2 -0.8 -2.3 -0.8`.
- `tools/abd.py` and `tools/gated.py`: the drafted run. One arm with drafts on, on the TTFT table's nine prompts,
  64 tokens at temperature 0; the gate requires drafts on, drafts accepted on every request, and equal replies.
- The only edit to the tools as run: the page-cache drop reads its command from `PT_DROP_CACHES`.

## Drafted runs

One server an arm, main then branch, drafts on at the family's own drafter, the TTFT table's nine prompts, 64
tokens at temperature 0, `--prompt-cache-gib 0`, page cache dropped before each server. Every request drafted and
had drafts accepted.

| Family | Drafter | Replies equal | Accepted / drafted, main | Cold TTFT branch vs main, 2K / 16K / 32K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 31B | DFlash, `z-lab/gemma-4-31B-it-DFlash` + copies | 9 of 9 | 40-49 of 97-192 | -9.2..-11.7 / -2.9..-6.8 / -3.8..-4.0 % |
| Nemotron 3.5 Lightning | its MTP head + copies | 9 of 9 | 29-36 of 39-49 | -1.0..+0.4 / -0.1..+0.4 / -0.4..0.0 % |

Nemotron's MTP head absorbs the prompt rows, so every chunk is read and runs whole: TTFT is level. Gemma 4's DFlash
drafter taps layers 1, 12, 23, 35, 46 and 57 of 60 (`target_layer_ids` in its config), not the last layer, so a
non-final chunk is still unread and stops at its last state write with the drafter on too; the replies are equal and
the TTFT gain holds. These are single arms, one server each, not a base, new, new, base run.

Drafted and accepted counts differ slightly on some prompts between the arms while the tokens are equal (Gemma 4 on
all nine, by up to 19 drafted and 1 accepted; Nemotron on one, 32 against 31 accepted). The cause was not
measured; there is no main against main control.

## Redaction

Local paths, user and host names are replaced (`redaction-report.json` counts them per file). Nemotron's
`prompt_lp.plp` (prompt_logprobs, about 3.7 MB an arm) is replaced by the sha256 of its sorted JSON and its row
count; the gate compared it in full. Everything else is as recorded. `SHA256SUMS` covers every other file here.
# Qwen CUDA first-token handoff on DGX Spark

This change delivers the committed first token before preparing the initial
speculative draft. On the tested Qwen3.8-27B/DFlash2 configuration it reduces
loaded-model time to first text. Draft computation still runs, and complete
response times and startup are not uniformly faster.

## Source and environment

- Baseline: PR836, `5e1c3feaa79e40f7659537d96b939129abe39df9`.
- Validation source: `fd306e82e020c1a58f160e247efd013441cfa826`.
  The publication uses the identical 13 changed source files; their SHA256s
  are in [evidence.json](evidence.json). CUDA kernels and build inputs are
  unchanged, and all 37 compiled CUDA fatbins match the baseline byte for byte.
- One NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10/SM121, 128 GB unified memory; Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS,
  aarch64. Host driver `580.178.04` (`nvidia-smi` CUDA line `13.0`, the
  driver ceiling). That driver string was recorded on this Spark on 16 October
  2026, and `/usr/bin/nvidia-smi` is dated 10 August 2026, before the 15 October
  runs. Kernel `7.0.0-1019-nvidia` was read on this Spark on 17 October 2026;
  it was not logged during the timing runs themselves.
- Both builds used `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.07-py3`, image
  `sha256:15b8de8baabe68e46afc51e88f3ccad5042013bafe8f244ec082ce0bb06d47e3`
  (created 2026-07-25), target `aarch64-linux-gnu.2.28`, Zig 0.17.0,
  ReleaseFast. The toolkit in that image is CUDA `13.3.1.008`. Its `nvcc` is
  release 13.3, V13.3.73 (`cuda_13.3.r13.3/compiler.38244171_0`), confirmed by
  running `nvcc --version` in the image on 17 October 2026. The host `nvcc`
  (13.0, V13.0.88) was not the compiler.
- Native server SHA256, shared by the loaded panel, both startup orders and
  the smoke runs: baseline
  `5700939fd17c0ad52a84c7d4bdbeeba7975a6c96952375579fda0a5d70c306c6`,
  candidate
  `e42ab4fc5079bfdeafe61234de4d044fec62e18877568e87fb19bb7e9523d581`.
  Each binary's source archive matches the baseline or candidate archive in
  [evidence.json](evidence.json).
- Target: `TensorFold/Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-4bit`, revision
  `70ae7fac63274ff2eac54152031433374cb80f2f`.
- Drafter: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, revision
  `50307d4c4cde6860d4eee73e2547cd786fe8e8a4`.
- BF16 KV, 32,768-token context, 16 server slots, zero restored prompt-cache
  tokens. Short timing requests are greedy with 256 generated tokens.
- The serving engine is Zig/CUDA. The checkpoint's MLX name identifies its
  storage format; the MLX runtime is not used for these measurements.

## Loaded-model results

The process order is baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline. Each number below
is the geometric mean of the two per-process medians for that arm. Percentage
changes use the geometric candidate/baseline ratio. These are descriptive
measurements from one ABBA sequence, not a statistical significance claim.

Fresh short requests:

| Case | Streams | TTFT, baseline → candidate (ms) | Decode, baseline → candidate (tok/s per stream) | Full response, baseline → candidate (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Coding | 1 | 131.9 → 119.1 | 53.94 → 53.96 | 4.860 → 4.845 |
| Coding | 4 | 326.2 → 316.4 | 25.08 → 25.77 | 10.400 → 10.181 |
| Coding | 16 | 1111.2 → 1102.6 | 6.10 → 6.40 | 42.682 → 40.583 |
| Chat | 1 | 144.5 → 136.5 | 33.70 → 32.92 | 7.712 → 7.884 |
| Chat | 4 | 338.9 → 324.0 | 18.89 → 19.24 | 13.862 → 13.624 |
| Chat | 16 | 1152.3 → 1138.6 | 5.45 → 5.41 | 47.556 → 48.209 |

Loaded short TTFT is 0.77–9.77% lower across all 12 fresh/repeat cells.
Beside that gain, fresh single-stream chat completion is 2.23% longer
(decode 2.32% lower) and fresh sixteen-stream chat completion is 1.37% longer.
This is delivery ordering after prefill. It is not faster prefill arithmetic
and it is not a startup speedup. All repeat-cell results and both original
observations are in [metrics.csv](metrics.csv), including the slower cases.

Fresh four/sixteen-stream batches contain distinct prompts. Repeated batches
send the same `s00` prompt to every stream after a primer, rather than repeating
each distinct fresh prompt. At one stream, fresh and repeated cell prompts are
identical. Neither arm restores cached tokens. Request IDs, counts and body
hashes are retained in the evidence file.

The evolving-history control uses a 4,419-token shared prefix and a 4,445-token
follow-up, with 32 output tokens. Initial/follow-up TTFT changes are -0.49% and
-0.65%; completion changes are +0.18% and +0.10%. This does not exercise a
prefix-cache acceleration path.

## Startup and remaining trade-offs

Each cell was measured in both baseline-first and candidate-first order after
restarting the server and loading the model. Readiness was roughly 27–30.5 s.
Filesystem cache state was warm or uncontrolled: these are process-cold tests,
not controlled storage-cold starts. No startup speedup is established.

| Case | Streams | Launch-to-ready change | Launch-to-first-text change | Launch-to-last-DONE change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Coding | 1 | +0.63% | +0.63% | +0.06% |
| Coding | 4 | +3.36% | +3.32% | +2.72% |
| Coding | 16 | +0.15% | -0.13% | +0.97% |
| Chat | 1 | -0.81% | -0.80% | -1.27% |
| Chat | 4 | +0.94% | +0.87% | +0.73% |
| Chat | 16 | -3.24% | -3.02% | -0.99% |

Lower latency changes are better. The first sixteen-stream chat request batch
after startup has 4.05% higher median request TTFT across the two orders.
Warm repeats within the startup experiment also vary: single-stream coding
has 5.19% lower measured decode and 5.21% longer completion; single-stream chat
has 4.10% lower decode and 3.96% longer completion. These cells use the startup
protocol and are separate from the loaded-model panel above. The CSV records
all first-request, warm-repeat and launch-inclusive measurements.

TTFT ends at the first nonempty text SSE; full response ends at DONE. Decode
is `(tokens - 1) / (last text arrival - first text arrival)`. Delivering the
first token earlier can lengthen that decode interval without making completion
later. Actual completion regressions also occur and are retained here.

Speculative work differs in 108/196 panel pairs, 48/90 forward startup pairs
and 49/90 reverse startup pairs. Unchanged-arm repeats also differ. These
receipts do not isolate a kernel or scheduler cause for the timing changes.
The reported prefill timing boundary moves with the handoff; it does not show
faster prefill arithmetic.

## Correctness and checks

- 376 paired timing requests match baseline/candidate request bodies, tokens
  and output hashes: 196 panel, 90 forward startup, 90 reverse startup.
  This includes served 1/4/16-stream comparisons and 40 anchor, primer,
  changed-prompt and longer-history control pairs beyond the 336 short pairs.
- Six additional smoke pairs pass. Sampled code/chat controls use temperature
  0.7, top-k 20, top-p 0.95 and seed 1234; draft-on/off output matches within
  and across arms. Sampled performance was not measured.
- Disconnect after the first text is followed by drained connections/waiting
  requests and a successful recovery request in both arms.
- Host fixtures cover commit/logprob uniqueness, cancellation at handoff,
  max-one/EOS cleanup, terminal trace/allocation failure, no requeue after
  an emitted token, and another job's draft failure while a terminal job lives.
- The qualified Spark candidate passed 483/483 host tests and built successfully.
  Local publication formatting and diff checks pass. The lean checker reports
  527 inherited findings on both baseline and candidate, with zero new findings;
  its nonzero exit is not described as a clean baseline.
- All four accepted model runs completed and restored the pre-existing service
  configuration. Minimum available memory was 61.31 GiB; the 8 GiB reserve held.
- No model/device qualification was run for Metal, Windows, other CUDA devices
  or other Qwen checkpoints. The long 2k/8k/32k/64k prefill ladder was not run;
  the served change concerns first-token delivery after prefill. No resumed
  cache path or image-input performance claim is made.

## Related work

This is a focused follow-up to BobClawblaw's PR836 Qwen CUDA engine and the
first-token work discussed in PR747, following the maintainer's invitation
to port focused changes. PR608 and PR726 provided the earlier engine and
integration work; their older performance figures are not used as this baseline.

PR853/PR888 change admission and prompt reuse, and PR861 changes planner paths;
integration must preserve their semantics and explicitly carry the callback
through any new admission path. PR928's adoption-mode fix and PR929's TCP_NODELAY
change are complementary. None of these changes is claimed by this receipt.

## What the GPU receipts show, and what they do not
