Q, dO and dQ are token-major `[rows, heads, width]`; K/V and their separate adjoints are canonical token-major
`[capacity, kv_heads, width]`. Head h reads KV head `h / (heads / kv_heads)`. All uses accumulate, including prefix
keys that have no answer loss themselves. The native head-major/paged caches need explicit adapters in a trainer.

Each query supplies its captured half-open logical range `[begin, end)`. It can describe global causal attention,
a sliding window or the upper bound that exposes all rows of an image block. These integer masks are fixed tape.
A linear snapshot starts at token 0. A ring snapshot owns `[first, first + capacity)`, with logical token t stored at
`t % capacity`. All query ranges must fit that one generation. A trainer retains earlier generations or a full
sequence tape before eviction; the host API does not reconstruct overwritten keys.

The function admits shapes, byte counts, windows, output/input/metadata aliases and selected input finiteness before
writing. It overwrites adjoints; unused cache rows stay zero and masked nonfinite inputs are never read.
Admission and allocation failures leave outputs unchanged. Nonfinite arithmetic during differentiation clears
all adjoints and returns an error.
Input arrays and mask metadata stay unchanged. K and V input aliases are allowed; their returned gradients remain
separate for the caller's chain rule.

```sh
zig build test-gemma4-attention-backward-host -j1 --summary all
```

The independent dense-mask binary64 objective has its own physical-to-logical mapping and forward loss.
Tiny linear and wrapped cases check every Q/K/V coordinate at three central step sizes in both f64 and f32.
Directional cases use the 31B's 32/16 heads at width 256 and 32/4 at width 512, and the 12B's 16/8 and 16/1 forms.
They cross 1,024-key windows, a 1,025-key extended upper bound, ring wrap and incomplete global tails.
Single-key, shared-head accumulation, synthetic input ties, repeat, ownership and allocation failures are separate
checks. FP64 slopes use `1e-8 + 1e-6 * abs(slope)`; FP32 uses `2e-7 + 3e-5 * abs(slope)`.
These are local host derivative-check limits. Whole-model acceptance and kernel/resource limits are unchanged.

This continuum model starts after Q/K/V preparation. Central slopes differentiate those continuous input nodes,
rather than a BF16 quantizer. CUDA's wide probability halves, split reductions, Metal's probability storage and
M5 operand cuts still need backend-specific forward tapes and contracts. The host check qualifies none of those
precision profiles, RMS/RoPE, the complete loss graph or checkpoint learning.

## Shared family, fitting and persistence

Use the shared Living Weights family descriptor, learner and shard writer, as for the dense Qwen pocket. The gate
in `living/pocket_save.zig` checks that saved gate/up/down values equal the accepted live values and retains pending
save state on failure. Extend the shared two-input neuron activation and its fit/rounding helpers to Gemma's
`gelu_pytorch_tanh` GeGLU before declaring the family. Tensor names and config scope must come from the admitted
Gemma namespace and geometry. This first step leaves that shared family table and save gate unchanged.

Start native learning qualification with MLX affine4/group64 and whole-group pocket widths. Reuse the dense widened
reader and original-column copy logic; keep the original packed weight, scale and bias bytes, tied head and config
fields exact. Give CUDA and Metal the same serialized family/tensor/quantization description and neuron ordering.
Reject unsupported learning formats by name before allocation. Serving keeps every format it already admits.

The future shared gate must round candidate neurons exactly as the writer will, evaluate the stored values, then
require held-out recall, earlier-fact retention, unrelated-fact checks and exact take-out/delete/rollback before
commit. Check saveBegin/saveFinish, cancellation, allocation and write failures through the real shared learner.
Its internal save reader handles pending state without reopening that folder through normal public admission.
Reopen each successful CUDA save on Metal and each Metal save on CUDA, with original tensor hashes retained.

## CUDA pocket and trainer

1. Separate shipped MLP columns from appended neurons at load. At the normalized pre-feedforward input, compute
   extra GeGLU neurons and add their down projection before post-feedforward normalization. Preserve sandwich
   norms and the learned layer scalar. Apply the same seam in prompt chunks, verification windows and decode.
   An empty pocket performs no new allocation, synchronization, readback or launch. An untaught stream reads
   the shipped columns even beside a taught stream.
2. Retain the actual serving forward's pre/post-normalization rows, scalar, GeGLU inputs, final normalized rows
   and capped-head nodes. Implement mean answer loss once and the tied head's input adjoint, including the exact
   softcap stores. Follow the full residual/sandwich-norm chain back to each requested pocket subject row.
3. Capture prepared Q/K/V and each query's actual lower/upper bound, position, rotary frequencies, cache owner
   and logical generation. Accumulate Q/K/V adjoints with the host formula as an independent mathematical check.
   Add the actual CUDA probability-half, context and projection cut conventions and independent local controls.
4. Pull Q/K back through learned RMS and the stored rotary table. Pull V back through unweighted RMS. On tied
   global layers, add both distinct preparation pullbacks into the shared raw K projection before its affine
   input adjoint. A prepared K buffer and a prepared V buffer represent different nodes despite that raw tie.
5. Qualify 31B and 12B separately. Per-layer-input and shared-KV-owner variants need their additional backward
   paths and owner accumulation before admission. Keep those learning configurations refused until then.

## Metal pocket and trainer

Use the same descriptor, fitting policy, saved tensor layout and acceptance path. Follow the dense Metal trainer's
buffer ownership and command-completion structure with Gemma operators. Keep training scratch separate from served
streams; retain captured rows until GPU completion, drain before publishing a replacement pocket, and invalidate
standing, draft and prompt-cache state after every edit. Carry each stream's untaught selection through every pass.

Implement native Metal backward stages for the saved Gemma forward. The host module remains a test oracle, never
an inference or training CPU fallback. Register each new operator's precision nodes, actual geometry, exceptional
classes, repeats, guards, accumulator witnesses and planted source controls. Keep unmeasured compiler/resource
records pending. Qualify pre-M5 and M5 independently, including their probability-product conventions.

## Gates before enabling native learning

Use a tiny nonzero Gemma-shaped model to compare the complete trainer and serving loss and directional gradients,
including prefix subject rows with no own loss, sliding/global transitions, GeGLU, sandwich norms, scalar and capped
head. Retain the existing whole-model directional rule, every failure and every refusal. A local ideal-attention
pass is only one component of that receipt.

Run CUDA and pre-M5/M5 cells with pinned binaries, runtime, model/tokenizer revisions, quantization, seeds and cache
settings. Require original-folder tokens and speed against main, drafted/plain equality, mixed taught/untaught
streams, all prompt cuts, image-boundary serving, resume/restart, rejection cleanup and the save round trip.
Measure learning time and peak host/device memory separately. This host step claims no real-model learning,
retention, device fidelity, speed or portability result.
# GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA

The native CUDA build serves GLM-5.3-Flash at tensor parallel over hosts: from NVIDIA's ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint
([1.0.12](../../CHANGELOG.md#1012)), on two ranks from Mia-AiLab's EXL3/TR3 checkpoint
([1.1.0](../../CHANGELOG.md#110), [the checkpoint](glm-5.3-flash.md#exl3)), and in [1.1.5](../../CHANGELOG.md#115) (#1050) from
NVIDIA's FP4-Local checkpoint as stored and from XSFP4, which keeps FP4-Local's tensors outside the routed experts.
Jammed XSFP4, in [1.2.3](../../CHANGELOG.md#123) ([#2041](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/2041)), holds those experts at block 32 in the `csf0_v1` form and loads the same way.
Rank 0 serves HTTP and the other ranks follow its steps, with MTP drafts, concurrent streams and kept prompt states.
The [Python 0.6.6 recipe](glm-5.3-flash.md) and its `--tp`, `--rank` and `--master` flags belong to the frozen engine.

## Run

`TF_GLM_RANK` of `TF_GLM_WORLD` places each rank, and `NCCL_COMM_ID` names rank 0's address and port on the link
between the hosts ([placement](../multi-rank-receipts.md)). Give every rank the same arguments: before the weights load
the ranks compare their settings, model and build, and name the field and rank that differ. `--context` takes a
positive limit for GLM. On two GB10s, with 192.0.2.1 as rank 0's address on their direct link:

```bash
tensorfold pull nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4@423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93
# on rank 1
TF_GLM_RANK=1 TF_GLM_WORLD=2 NCCL_COMM_ID=192.0.2.1:29583 \
  tensorfold serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --context 245760 --parallel 1
# on rank 0 (192.0.2.1)
TF_GLM_RANK=0 TF_GLM_WORLD=2 NCCL_COMM_ID=192.0.2.1:29583 \
  tensorfold serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --context 245760 --parallel 1
```

Set `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` and `NCCL_IB_HCA` for the link between the hosts as NCCL documents them. Each rank keeps a
TCP line to rank 0 on the port after `NCCL_COMM_ID`'s (29584 here), opened before NCCL: a rank that fails, refuses or
dies stops the others.

The contributed runs read that revision. The repository's later commit `da920bb0`, which declares the MTP layer as
BF16 in the quantization ignore lists, was not among them. On shipped 1.1.0 these settings loaded the whole checkpoint
in 302.1 s, and rank 0 reported `model 96.11 GiB; 1 stream at once, 3.16 GiB each at a 245760-token window, of 5.8 GiB
left after a 12.2 GiB reserve` and a 5.8 GiB prompt cache
([#1040](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1040)).

## Requests

- `--vision` on every rank reads images and video: rank 0's tower encodes them and sends their rows and spans to the
  other ranks ([1.1.0](../../CHANGELOG.md#110)). Video needs `libtfvideo`
  ([video](../vision.md#video-on-the-native-server)). `TF_GLM_VISION_HOST=1` keeps the tower's bf16 weights in pinned
  host memory and copies each part of a pass into one device slot as it runs (240 MiB for GLM-5.3-Flash's tower instead
  of its 1.05 GiB), leaving rank 0 that much more room for KV pages. Checked on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards.
- Nonstreaming `/v1/completions` requests return `prompt_logprobs`, structured output follows its schema with drafts
  on, and required and named tool calls use the model's tool markup ([1.1.1](../../CHANGELOG.md#111): #1016 to #1018).
- `--kv-cache fp8` is an opt-in FP8 latent cache. BF16 remains the default, and its native quality and device
  qualification are pending ([1.1.2](../../CHANGELOG.md#112)).
- `TF_GLM_HOST_CACHE=1` on every rank keeps kept prompt states in pinned host memory instead of on the card, so a
  long conversation's next turn resumes when the card has no room left for its state (#1510). `--prompt-cache-gib`
  sizes the host cache on each rank (8 GiB unasked, at most half of the available memory), and the KV pool sets no
  device cache aside. Checked on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards at TP=2 with the EXL3 4bpw checkpoint.
- A kept state larger than the prompt cache's whole budget is not kept (`kept nothing at … passes the … budget` on the
  log), so a long conversation's next turn runs its prompt again from the start. With KV pages, `TF_KV_SHARE=n` keeps a
  prompt's rows as the pool's pages instead of copying them into the cache, and that log line names it.
- With KV pages (the default at two or more ranks), the pool sets the windows the room holds aside before the prompt
  cache, which gets what they leave of its 16 GiB. `--prompt-cache-gib N` sets N GiB aside first, after the engine's
  own window and a fixed part and page for each other stream, and the pool takes the rest.
- `TF_GLM_PROMPT_TAIL=1` keeps a prompt that names no history, as a `/v1/completions` request's, at its last prompt
  chunk start, as a chat keeps its history's, so the same prompt or a longer one resumes there. Those states share the
  prompt cache's budget with chat states, least recently used out first, so long raw prompts between two chat turns can
  push the chat's state out. Unset or 0, a raw prompt keeps none; GLM refuses any other value at startup. The KV
  pages' store (`TF_KV_SHARE`) keeps a prompt's last page either way.
- `TF_GLM_KV_HOST=1` on every rank (with KV pages, BF16) keeps the KV pages' latent rows in pinned host memory: the
  device keeps the pooled index keys, and each sparse call copies only the rows it picked into device slots. The KV
  pool then costs the card 768 bytes a token instead of 13,056, so a 1,048,576-token window fits beside the weights.
  `TF_GLM_KV_HOST_GIB` sizes the host pages (one full window unasked); `TF_GLM_KV_HOST_SHARED=1` gives the ranks of
  one host a single copy in `/dev/shm`. Checked on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell cards at TP=2.
- `TF_KV_SHARE=n` (with KV pages, 64 at most) keeps prompts' rows as the pool's pages, and the startup plan sets aside
  a slot for each of the n kept states' other parts in the prompt cache, as many as the cache holds; the rest of the
  cache goes to the pool's pages. `--prompt-cache-gib N` bounds them: the startup line names the slots, and when the
  cache holds fewer than n, how many it holds and the `--prompt-cache-gib` that holds all n.
- `TF_GLM_CHUNK_SOLO=4096` on every rank (opt-in) lets a prompt pass take 4,096 rows while no other stream is decoding.
  Unset or `2048`, every pass takes 2,048 rows and nothing extra is held. See [Prompt chunk size](#prompt-chunk-size).
- `TF_GLM_DENSE_BITS=4` (EXL3 at TP=2, off by default) repacks the BF16 dense layers to 4 bits at load. Decode is
  faster (24.8 to 35.0 tok/s in one user's run), but replies differ from the default, so it is lossy and stays opt-in
  (#1761).

## Verified copy drafts

`TF_GLM_COPIES=1` on rank 0 tries the lane host's cost-priced root/context copies, with a four-token history match.
Unset or 0 retains the existing policy. Copies use the normal target verify/partial-keep path and require no external
drafter; `--no-drafts` and `"draft": false` remain plain. The inherited target-cost tables seed pricing and observed
copy rejections can cut an offer to zero rows. The opt-in's head confidence is a maximum prefix; cost may choose plain.
See [copy pricing and the required TP=2 comparison](cuda-lane-copies.md#glm-on-cuda). Device exactness and speed are
pending, so keep the default policy until that checkpoint's complete cost and reply checks pass (#1910).

## More ranks

With `TF_GLM_PREFILL_REDUCE=ring`, the startup peer warm-up touches only each rank's next and previous neighbours,
using the existing rank order. The default split and gather modes still warm every peer. This removes the eager
opposite-peer warm-up; it does not add a switchless RoCE relay or qualify a four-node ring (#1971).

`TF_GLM_WORLD=3` places a third rank the same way. From 1.1.2 the uneven KDA input projections of TP=3 (22, 21 and
21 heads) run instead of being refused; TP=3 device qualification is pending
([#1067](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1067)). How a prompt's rows reach the other ranks
(`TF_GLM_PREFILL_REDUCE`) and the two-rank RoCE gathers (`TF_ROCE`) are in
[placement](../multi-rank-receipts.md#the-settings-the-ranks-agreed-on).

## Prompt chunk size

A prompt runs in passes of 2,048 rows. Kept prompt states sit on that grid, and a stream decoding beside a prompt waits
for each pass to end. A pass that takes more rows reads each routed expert's weights fewer times, so a lone prompt
comes sooner. `TF_GLM_CHUNK_SOLO=4096` lets a pass take two of those chunks when no other stream is decoding as it
starts. With one decoding, or with `prompt_logprobs` or image rows, the pass takes 2,048. Beside `--drafter`, DFlash2
reads a solo pass's taps whole and keeps the prompt's last 2,048 rows as before; its tap buffer holds 4,096 rows, 80 MiB
more on each rank. Solo passes take the place of `TF_GLM_PROMPT_PAIR`'s paired steps, whose second set of buffers they
do not hold.

The grid does not move, so warm turns resume where they do unset, and streams decoding beside a prompt see the same
passes. Replies are the same bytes either way. Two costs remain:
- A request that arrives during a solo pass waits for that pass to end before its own prompt runs. After that, the
  passes are short again.
- The prompt buffers are sized for 4,096 rows for the whole run: 1.92 GiB more at TP=2 and 1.56 GiB at TP=3 (and
  DFlash2's 80 MiB), which comes out of the room for KV pages and the prompt cache. In the runs below, TP=2's default cache goes from 4.7 to
  2.8 GiB.

| | TP=2 unset | TP=2 `=4096` | TP=3 unset | TP=3 `=4096` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First token of a cold prompt, 8K / 32K / 128K (s) | 6.08 / 23.94 / 98.16 | 5.72 / 22.22 / 91.33 | 5.00 / 19.61 / 80.26 | 4.64 / 17.99 / 73.45 |
| First token of a warm turn, 10K history + 500 / 1,500 / 3,000 tokens (s) | 1.40 / 2.06 / 2.87 | 1.40 / 2.05 / 2.83 | 1.14 / 1.67 / 2.35 | 1.14 / 1.68 / 2.31 |
| First token of a warm turn, 40K history + 500 / 1,500 / 3,000 tokens (s) | 1.25 / 2.03 / 3.05 | 1.26 / 2.04 / 3.03 | 1.02 / 1.67 / 2.51 | 1.02 / 1.66 / 2.48 |
| Gap between a decoding stream's tokens beside a 32K prompt, median / longest (ms) | 1,474 / 1,749 | 1,478 / 1,751 | 1,219 / 1,444 | 1,219 / 1,459 |
| That stream's tokens during the prompt | 17.0 | 16.5 | 16.0 | 16.5 |
| First token of a short request sent 6 to 8 s into a 32K prompt, mean (lowest to highest) (s) | 1.27 (0.88 to 1.65) | 2.48 (1.35 to 3.47) | 1.24 (0.70 to 1.67) | 1.73 (1.07 to 2.67) |
| That prompt's first token (s) | 23.54 | 23.27 | 19.32 | 18.99 |

Each setting is two fresh servers (one at TP=2 for the cold row), `--parallel 4 --context 524288`, `TF_KV_PAGES=on`,
`Bizuayeu/GLM-5.3-Flash-XSFP4` with its MTP drafts. Cold prompts are Python source at `--prompt-cache-gib 0`, and a
repeated filler line gains 2 to 5% at the same sizes. The other rows ran with the prompt cache on (the default at TP=2,
2 GiB at TP=3). Three rows at TP=2 that waited on the heat guard are left out.

It doesn't pay with every checkpoint. With `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` on two GB10s at `--parallel 1 --context 65536`,
`=4096` made cold prompts slower: 8K and 32K prompts ran 12 to 14% slower (about 1,280 against 1,480 tok/s at 8K), and
the model took 1.9 GiB more at startup. That's two fresh servers each, with the same tokens either way. Leave it unset
there.

At TP=3 with `TF_GLM_ROCE_MULTI=1` (#1524) the gain is a little under half: on three GB10s at `--parallel 8` with
`TF_KV_SHARE=32` and `TENSORFOLD_PREFILL_SHARE=0.7`, not the table's settings, cold Python-source prompts of 8K to
128K tokens came 3.2 to 3.4% sooner with the wire and 7.3 to 8.4% sooner without it, two fresh servers each. The wire's
extra time is in the side stream's exchanges and grows when solo doubles a pass (#1994). `TF_GLM_OVERLAP_PIECES`
(1 to 8, the same on every rank; unset, 8 when `TF_GLM_CHUNK_SOLO=4096` and `TF_GLM_ROCE_MULTI=1` are both set at three
ranks or more, where the wire opens, and 3 otherwise) cuts a prompt chunk's exchanges into that many row pieces.
In a further run
at those settings, solo on the wire came 1.7 to 3.6% sooner at 3 pieces and 6.1 to 7.8% sooner at 8, against the wire
without solo at 3, with the same tokens; in another, 8 pieces without solo stayed within 1% of 3 (#1994).

## Long runs on GB10

Long prompts and long runs of replies heat a GB10. The runbook's [heat bands](../../RUNBOOK.md#linux-and-cuda) (with a
1,035,295-token prompt at TP=3), [CPU pinning](../../RUNBOOK.md#gb10-cpu-pinning-for-long-cuda-runs) and
[GPU clock cap](../../RUNBOOK.md#gb10-gpu-clock-cap-for-long-cuda-runs) each carry a measured GLM-5.3-Flash run.
# GLM-5.3-Flash

This recipe describes the Python 0.6.6 engine, available at the
[`v0.6.6` tag](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/tree/v0.6.6).
Its CUDA EXL3 reader, two-rank flags and DFlash2 policies do not apply to the native Zig binary.
Nor do its Mac settings. The native binary refuses `--ssd-experts` and reads `GLM_LOAD_LIMIT_GB` (in GB) where this
page uses `TENSORFOLD_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB` (in GiB); the `TF_GLM_*` variables and the Python paths and modules below are
that engine's too, except `TF_GLM_CLEAR_THINKING`, which the native server also reads ([api](../api.md)).
The native binary serves GLM on two M5 Ultra Macs with MLX affine 4-bit/group-64 weights, and on CUDA ranks from
NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint and the EXL3/TR3 checkpoint ([GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA](glm-5.3-flash-cuda.md)).
For native serving, use the [qualified model table](../../README.md#pick-a-model), the
[paired Metal runbook](../../RUNBOOK.md#flash-next-and-paired-metal-serving) and that page.
@chadhurley25075-png wrote the Mac family in [#9](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/9), with fixes from
@kingjamez, and its prompt path in [#39](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/39); the native engine runs
the decode kernels of #9. [Credits](../credits.md) names the contributors to the CUDA engine and the Mac options below.

The `glm5_next` family serves `TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP` on two-rank CUDA and, on a Mac with
256 GB, on the MLX lane engine ([Apple Silicon](#apple-silicon-mlx)).
The checkpoint uses affine 4-bit weights in groups of 64 and includes its MTP layer.
Kimi delta attention, sparse MLA and MoE blocks mix four residual streams.

## CUDA

On CUDA GLM-5.3-Flash runs on two ranks from Brandon M. Music's EXL3/TR3 checkpoint
(`brandonmusic/GLM-5.3-Flash-tr3-4bpw`, re-hosted as `Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-TR3-4bpw`; experimental;
[EXL3](#exl3)) or from the MLX 4-bit checkpoint, the portable option that a 256 GB Mac serves too.
No NVFP4 checkpoint of it is read. `tensorfold serve` loads the checkpoint you name; it picks none by itself. Prompt
precision does not change here: neither checkpoint has an FP8 prompt kernel, so `--prefill-fp8` is refused.

Use the [Python two-rank setup](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/blob/v0.6.6/RUNBOOK.md#nvidia-gpus)
but replace its unpinned installation command with the Python
[0.6.6 release revision](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/tag/v0.6.6) below.
An unpinned install selects the native default branch, which does not serve this CUDA recipe.
Verify that `tensorfold --version` reports `0.6.6`, then pull the same checkpoint on both ranks:

```bash
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold.git@cb2ebf0540f42604e2759b2ddef497861e928248"
tensorfold --version
tensorfold pull TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP
tensorfold serve TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP --tp 2 --rank 1 --master 192.0.2.1
tensorfold serve TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP --tp 2 --rank 0 --master 192.0.2.1 --name bench --host 0.0.0.0
```

Rank 1 starts first and rank 0 serves HTTP. Use the same context and drafting settings on both ranks.
The optional `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` model has CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms; pull it on both ranks only
when those terms fit the intended use. The CLI uses it automatically once it has been pulled.
Without it, the engine uses MTP drafts; `--drafter none` explicitly selects MTP-only drafting.
Give both ranks the same drafter setting. `--no-drafts` disables all drafting for the serial reference.
A checkpoint with neither an MTP head nor a supplied DFlash2 model is refused unless drafts are disabled.
`TF_GLM_MTP` decides whether the CUDA engine loads the MTP head: `1` (the default) keeps it beside DFlash2, so MTP
policies and `auto`'s per-round choice stay available; `auto` leaves it out when DFlash2 is loaded or drafts are
disabled; `0` leaves it out. Left out, it saves each rank the head's weights (about 2 GiB for this checkpoint), its
cache rows and decode buffers, and prompts skip its absorb; MTP policies (and `--mtp-drafts N`) then draft with
DFlash2. Replies are the same either way. On two GB10s with DFlash2, `auto` read prompts about 3% faster and decoded
sampled code faster, but greedy chat about 4% slower, so the head stays by default. Give both ranks the same setting.

### EXL3

Brandon M. Music created this EXL3/TR3 checkpoint (`brandonmusic/GLM-5.3-Flash-tr3-4bpw`, ShapleyMCG License 1.0,
which asks for attribution); `Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-TR3-4bpw` is a byte-identical re-host of it. Either ID
serves. It is an experimental CUDA checkpoint. The reader supports 4-bit
mcg-codebook routed experts with BF16 weights elsewhere, not arbitrary EXL3 layouts. Start it with the
two-rank command above, substituting its checkpoint ID on both ranks. With DFlash2 available, the EXL3
`auto` policy uses DFlash2; without it, MTP remains available.

The expert decoder and BF16 target matmul keep row arithmetic fixed. A quantized copy of the head may
propose drafts, but target verification retains the BF16 head. EXL3 speed, capacity and long-context
qualification are TBD [release-0.3.5].

### Draft policies

For the affine checkpoint with its MTP head loaded, the default `auto` policy uses MTP for sampled requests.
For greedy requests with DFlash2 loaded beside the head (`TF_GLM_MTP=1`, the default),
it compares committed tokens per estimated round time and chooses a drafter. It periodically probes
the other drafter and discards its old rate after switching away, so later probes can change the choice.
Without the head (`TF_GLM_MTP=auto` beside DFlash2, or `0`), `auto` drafts with DFlash2.
Every policy verifies against the same target, and `"draft": false` selects the serial reference.
A request can select a policy after `@` in its model ID, such as `bench@c3:0.35`, or with `tf_policy`.
`--mtp-drafts N` selects a fixed depth at startup. With DFlash2 available, `--mtp-drafts 0` selects
`fc5:0.3`; without it, zero selects the serial reference.

| Policy | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | Default per-request selection |
| `0` | Serial |
| `N` | Fixed number of MTP drafts |
| `a:LOW:HIGH` | MTP depth from running acceptance |
| `cN:P` | MTP chain capped at N and a probability-product threshold |
| `fN`, `fcN:P`, `fa:...` | Corresponding DFlash2 policies, requiring its checkpoint |

The default context is 2,051 tokens, where attention stays dense. A larger positive `--context` enables
sparse attention beyond that boundary if the startup memory estimate admits it on both ranks.
`--context 0` instead targets the affordable native window. An explicit reply reservation beyond the allocated window receives HTTP 400 before streaming; an omitted reply limit
is capped to the remaining space. Larger-context restart advice appears only when the estimate allows it.

Prompt prefill uses the shared CUDA prefill kernels. Decode uses CUDA graphs, past the dense limit one per
pool bucket. The engine keeps up to 8 conversations' prompts (`TF_GLM_CACHE_ENTRIES`): when another
conversation takes the attention caches, a kept prompt's rows are saved. Kept states and saved rows together get
`TF_GLM_CACHE_GIB` (default 3), or less when the window leaves less memory on either Spark; the startup log says
when it is less, and the memory estimate includes it. Earlier turns keep their reasoning in the prompt
(`clear_thinking` false, zai-org's default), so an agent's next user message resumes from its previous tool loop
instead of filling it again; `TF_GLM_CLEAR_THINKING=1` drops it, as the TR3 checkpoint's template does by default,
and a request's `chat_template_kwargs.clear_thinking` overrides either for that request. It serves one request at a
time. Both ranks finish a started reply after a client disconnects.

DFlash2 attends only its 2,048-row sliding window: a block pass reads only the window's tiles, and the drafter keeps
its context in a ring of that window, its block and a tile (2,176 rows, 21 MiB a rank whatever the window, instead
of 10 KiB a rank for every token of the window). A kept prompt DFlash2 can resume from holds a copy of the window
(20 MiB a rank, within `TF_GLM_CACHE_GIB`). The drafts are the same bits. `TF_GLM_DRAFT_RING=0` keeps the
whole-window buffer instead (give both ranks the same value). The memory estimate counts the draft model as it is
held (4-bit copies and its selector's codebooks, 0.63 GiB a rank), not at 4 bytes a checkpoint value.

### Long contexts: the latent cache

@taussoe built this cache in [#54](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/54).
The DSA layers are NoPE MLA: head h's key is `Wk_h c` and its value `Wv_h c`, with `c` the token's 512-wide
normalized latent and `Wk_h`, `Wv_h` blocks of `kv_b_proj`. So `score_h = (Wk_h^T q_h) . c` and
`out_h = Wv_h (sum_j p_j c_j)`. The CUDA engine caches `c` only (bf16, 1 KB a token and layer, shared by the
heads and both ranks; `TF_GLM_LATENT=0` returns to per-head keys and values), absorbs the query once per row,
attends over latents and expands the attended latent once. Past 2,051 tokens a row attends to its top 512 index
pools (2,048 tokens) plus its incomplete pool; the pools are ranked by one radix-select kernel over the pools the
chunk can see, rounded up to a power of two. Every kernel computes a row alone in an order fixed by its own
position, so a decode window's rows keep the serial steps' bits; prompt chunks give the same bits for any
chunking. The memory estimate sizes the latent cache (`mla_geometry(latent=True)`).

Measured on two DGX Sparks (GB10, 128 GB each) with the MLX 4-bit checkpoint, MTP drafts only,
`--context 262144`, a synthetic codebase with one hidden fact, cold prompts:

| Prompt | Prompt reading | First token | Decode at that depth | Hidden fact |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |
| 32,770 tokens | 1,138 tok/s | 29 s | 50.9 tok/s | found |
| 131,074 tokens | 898 tok/s | 146 s | 47.2 tok/s | found |
| 261,906 tokens | 849 tok/s | 309 s | 31.9 tok/s | found |

An earlier run of the same kernels read 131k and 256k prompts at 1,002 and 1,006 tok/s and decoded at 40.2 tok/s
at 256k; runs vary with page migration on the Sparks. Through the 256k prompt the torch peak stayed at 93.7 GiB
against a 96.1 GiB estimate, the kept conversations' 1.6 GiB included. MemAvailable never fell below 9.5 GiB;
the admission reserve (a tenth of RAM) also carries 3.5-4.8 GiB of CUDA context, NCCL and graph memory outside
the estimate. Drafted replies equaled serial ones (9/9, 2k to 16k), resumed prompts equaled fresh ones (6/6),
and four interleaved conversations each equaled their solo replies. `--context 0` allocated a 487,495-token
window, not measured that far.

Short prompts, with the recipe's default drafting (DFlash2, `auto`), decode at 53.8 / 43.4 / 85.0 / 50.0 tok/s
(code and chat, sampled and greedy, 64 tokens, median of 5 seeds) against 0.3.6's 53.4 / 44.1 / 63.7 / 45.5. The
latent path rounds attention differently, so some replies differ from 0.3.6 (the greedy cells' texts, hence their
speeds); `TF_GLM_LATENT=0` gives 0.3.6's replies exactly.

## Apple Silicon (MLX)

On a Mac with 256 GB and MLX 0.32.2 or later (`serve` refuses an older MLX):

```bash
tensorfold pull TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP
tensorfold serve TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP
```

The chat template names `low`, `high` and `max`. GLM's default is Max, and `high` suits agent and coding work.
`medium` is heard as `high`. `max` stays `max`. `xhigh` stays `xhigh`, and this template renders both as Max.
`--reasoning-effort high` selects High, and `--reasoning-effort low` selects Low.

The model decodes through the lane engine's family rounds with the checkpoint's MTP head. A round's drafted rows
are verified in one forward, and every row of a window gets its one-row call's bits, so drafted replies equal
`"draft": false`. A load-time check sets the widest exact window (up to 16 rows) and a second one whether several
streams' rows can share a forward; concurrent requests share rounds when it passes. The family sets
`MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0`, so M5-generation GPUs keep fp32 matmuls in fp32. Prompts prefill in the engine's chunks and a
resumed prompt gets a fresh prompt's bits.

The weights take about 170 GiB, so the family states an 85% memory allowance on Macs of 256 GB or less, for a
machine with nothing else loaded; concurrent streams are still admitted within it less what other programs hold.
Prompt admission counts the latent cache's growth and a prompt chunk's indexer workspace.

The load-time checks narrow the window or stop sharing forwards where bits would differ (on the CPU, where
nothing serves, a mixed-bit checkpoint's window narrows to 7 rows). Real-weight qualification on the 0.3.5 line,
against mlx-vlm 0.7.3's server (mlx_lm has no GLM-5.3-Flash), is TBD [release-0.3.5.1].

### Experts on SSD

`--ssd-experts GIB` leaves the decoder layers' routed experts (159.5 GiB of the 169.2) in the checkpoint and
streams them into a GPU pool of that many GiB. Everything else stays resident, the MTP layer included. With it,
a 128 GB Mac can serve GLM-5.3-Flash:

```bash
python -m pip install "tensorfold[ssd]"       # cmake and nanobind, to build a small MLX extension on first use
tensorfold serve TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP --ssd-experts 64
```

- After each layer's router, the GPU signals the host through a shared Metal event and waits.
- The host reads the picks and copies any expert missing from the pool from SSD into a free slot. It then
  updates the slot table and lets the GPU go on.
- The expert kernels are the resident ones with only the weight address changed, so replies are the
  resident model's tokens.
- A prompt chunk loads each layer's picked experts in turn.
- The pool keeps the most recently used experts, and reads bypass the page cache.
- The extension builds against the installed MLX with the Xcode command line tools.

On an M3 Ultra running the Python engine, held to a 128 GB Mac's budget (TENSORFOLD_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB=89.6) with
`--ssd-experts 64`, the streamed run was compared with the resident one on the same machine:
- Replies were the same tokens: 36 of 36 serial and cell requests, plus the 2k prompt.
- Two concurrent streams each matched their solo reply, and resumed prompts matched fresh ones.
- The footprint peaked at 87.6 GiB against 184.0 resident.
- Decode ran at 8.9-10.5 tok/s against 62.8-73.6 resident.
- A 2k prompt prefilled at 144 tok/s against 451.

### Mixed-bit checkpoints

The loader reads two layouts of the same weights: the original one (`TensorFold/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-4bit-MTP`) and the
one mlx-lm's converter writes (`language_model.model.*`, one fused `conv1d`, `forget_gate.*`, the absorbed
`embed_q` / `unembed_out` pair in place of `kv_b_proj`, the MTP layer as `mtp.0.*` with a bf16 `eh_proj`). Such
conversions usually store per-tensor overrides: routed experts at 4 bits, attention, shared experts and the head at
8, some layers at 5 or 6.
[`layouts.py`](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/blob/v0.6.6/src/tensorfold/families/glm5_next/layouts.py)
maps the names, a stack of parts at different widths runs part by part, and
8-, 6- and 5-bit tensors take row kernels transcribed from MLX's one-row `qmv_fast` / `qmv_quad` loops, so verify
windows keep one-row bits. On grant-ai's abliterated conversion, on a 256 GB M3 Ultra, the contributor measured
46.3 tok/s drafted, equal to `"draft": false`.

### Float32 activations

@feni6 added this mode in [#118](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/118).
Set `"tensorfold_activation_dtype": "float32"` in a checkpoint's `config.json` to run the residual stream, the MLA
latent and indexer caches and the KDA states in float32 instead of bf16. The hyper-connection split, the gated-delta
recurrence and the templated one-row GEMVs (`matmul_rows`) run their Metal kernels in float32. Quantized `qmv_rows`
stays on its bf16 kernel, so a float32 row uses MLX's one-row call. The fused KDA step, the sparse-decode attention
and the fused bf16 matrix kernels step aside for their MLX-op paths. Rows keep their bits, so drafted replies still
equal `"draft": false`, and without the key nothing changes (bf16 logits are byte-identical to before).

On an M3 Ultra with the resident 4-bit checkpoint, float32 activations decode at about 6-9 tok/s against
48-57 for bf16, and prefill is about 1.2-1.4x slower, so the mode is for quality work, not speed.

Measured on a 512 GB M3 Ultra with GLM-5.3-Flash converted losslessly from a Q8_0 GGUF, against a float64
reference of the same weights on 579 held-out items (MMLU-Pro 200, BBH 200, HumanEval 50, MBPP 129; per-item
token-weighted RMS difference of mean NLL):

| activations | BBH | HumanEval | MBPP | MMLU-Pro answers equal to the reference | prefill 4k / 32k tok/s | decode @32k tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bf16 | 0.219 | 0.016 | 0.038 | 187 / 200 | 365 / 338 | 20.4 |
| float32 | 0.011 | 0.002 | 0.003 | 199 / 200 | 371 / 312 | 19.6 |

llama.cpp's Metal path on the same Q8_0 weights (F32 KV cache) measured 0.073 / 0.016 / 0.035 and 190 / 200.
Memory: the caches double in size and admission counts them at 4 bytes a value; the weights are unchanged.
The CUDA engine refuses the key. `--ssd-experts` stays on the bf16 expert kernels and refuses this mode.

### 8-bit from a Q8_0 GGUF, without loss

@feni6 added 8-bit group-32 checkpoints and this converter in [#119](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/119).
A Q8_0 block (32 int8 values, one fp16 scale d) is exactly MLX's affine 8-bit format in groups of 32 with
q + 128, scale d and bias −128·d. `tools/glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx.py` converts llama.cpp's `glm5next` Q8_0 GGUF this
way; the tensors llama.cpp keeps unquantised (the indexer and KDA low-rank projections) stay unquantised, and the KDA
decay rate is stored as `A`. The Mac engine reads the result: fp16 scales are widened to float32 once at load, and
every projection returns its input's dtype.

```bash
python tools/glm5_q8_0_gguf_to_mlx.py --gguf 'GLM-5.3-Flash-Q8_0-*.gguf' \
    --config zai-org-GLM-5.3-Flash/config.json --tokenizer-dir zai-org-GLM-5.3-Flash --out GLM-5.3-Flash-q8_0 --verify
tensorfold serve GLM-5.3-Flash-q8_0
```

On a 512 GB M3 Ultra, a 310 GiB Q8_0 GGUF became 328.5 GiB in 85 shards in about six minutes; `--verify` found every
one of its 1,383 tensors equal to the GGUF's values. The weights take 365 GiB resident; the GGUF has no MTP layer, so
the model decodes without drafts. The group-32 8-bit layers run MLX's one-row calls, not the fused 4-bit kernels.

### Prefill

Prompt chunks attend as decode does: each query reads its own selected keys from the latent cache, so prefill cost
and memory stay flat with context. @chadhurley25075-png, who wrote it in
[#39](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/pull/39), measured 336 / 334 / 309 tok/s at 10k / 35k / 103k tokens on a
256 GB M3 Ultra, against 331 / 260 / 143 for the previous prefill.

### Scripts that load the backbone directly

`tensorfold serve` wires the weights (`mx.set_wired_limit`,
[`server/residency.py`](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/blob/v0.6.6/src/tensorfold/server/residency.py)) and caps
MLX's cache of freed
buffers. A script that calls `families.glm5_next.weights.load_backbone` directly, such as a scorer reading logits
or a profiler, should do the same: without wiring, macOS pages parts of a 170-365 GiB checkpoint out between steps, and
on a 512 GB M3 Ultra each MoE layer then took about 0.1 s per call (4.3 s per decode step instead of 0.1 s); with the
wired limit set to the whole working set and no cache cap, the cache of per-request buffers was wired too and grew
past 440 GiB. Wire what is resident after loading, cap the cache, and clear it between requests:

```python
import mlx.core as mx
from tensorfold.families.glm5_next.weights import load_backbone
from tensorfold.server.residency import wire_resident

info = mx.device_info()
mx.set_wired_limit(int(info["max_recommended_working_set_size"]))   # as the family's load() does
model = load_backbone(model_dir)
wire_resident(mx, int(info["max_recommended_working_set_size"]))   # then only the weights stay wired
mx.set_cache_limit(8 * 2**30)                                       # the server's --mlx-cache-gib default
# ... per request: run, then mx.clear_cache()
```

## Responses and exactness

When thinking is disabled, the server closes the template's open think block so the response reaches
`content`. Both servers turn GLM's native `arg_key`/`arg_value` tool calls into OpenAI `tool_calls`,
decoding each value by the tool's schema (a string keeps its exact text); the CUDA server keeps Qwen's XML
parameter values as text.

CUDA tests cover row arithmetic, recurrent rollback and synthetic model execution. Validate real
weights separately for drafted/serial and resumed/fresh output, with both thinking modes.
CUDA graphs and eager execution must agree under the same rank configuration.
Use a separate fp32 reference for quality checks, with TF32 disabled on that reference.

## Measurements

Use the [public benchmark command](README.md#measurements) with the server above. Retain model and
runtime revisions with every run. Decode rate, cold/resumed first-token latency and peak memory are
TBD [release-0.3.5]. Record the selected drafter policy with the result.
# GLM-OCR on HIP

The native HIP engine serves the BF16 `zai-org/GLM-OCR` checkpoint at
revision `2e85a62840ccac27daa451df36c736c4636b8628`, with no Python or
libtorch in the served engine. It was qualified with Zig 0.17.0 on a
Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201). An idle card is not required; native
admission checks current free memory.

## Build and start

Use a coherent ROCm tree, including its compiler and device bitcode:

```sh
zig build -Dhip=true -Dhip-arch=gfx1201 \
  -Dhipcc=/opt/rocm/core/bin/hipcc \
  -Dhip-device-lib=/opt/rocm/core/lib/llvm/amdgcn/bitcode \
  native-hip -j4 --summary all
```

The engine loads external native libraries at run time. Keep AOTriton
0.11.1 with its adjacent `aotriton.images` directory; its gfx120x images
are required for this GPU. libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1 keeps JPEG decoding
equal to the reference. MIOpen keeps its find database in the user
directory below, so set it to persistent storage.

```sh
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<ordinal>
export TENSORFOLD_AOTRITON=<aotriton>/lib/libaotriton_v2.so.0.11.1
export TENSORFOLD_LIBTURBOJPEG=<libjpeg-turbo>/lib64/libturbojpeg.so
export MIOPEN_USER_DB_PATH=<miopen-db>
export MIOPEN_CUSTOM_CACHE_DIR="$MIOPEN_USER_DB_PATH"

zig-out/native-hip/bin/tensorfold-native serve <GLM-OCR checkpoint> \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18897 --name glm-ocr --vision \
  --context 8192 --parallel 2 --prompt-cache-gib 1 --mtp-drafts 0 \
  --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --no-update-check --idle-unload 0
```

For a cache-off control, use a separate process and port with
`--prompt-cache-gib 0`. Leave the shared chat-template defaults in
place. The model returns OCR in `content`; its template's thinking
variable does not make it a reasoning model.

Structured JSON uses the existing optional grammar runtime. Build it
with `zig build grammar -Dxgrammar=<xgrammar source> --prefix <prefix>`
from the official xgrammar v0.2.8 source, and place
`libtfgrammar.so` in `zig-out/native-hip/lib`, beside the executable's
`bin` directory.

## Requests and checks

Send normal OpenAI chat-completion requests to `/v1/chat/completions`.
Use an `image_url` part containing a PNG, JPEG or WebP data URL and a
text part such as `Text Recognition:`, `Formula Recognition:` or
`Table Recognition:`. Greedy decoding and the original image bytes are
the reference settings. The default GLM image budget is 6,144 tokens,
which includes the original bee photo.

`tools/zig/glm_ocr_reference.py` is the one Python reference script.
Its `examples` subcommand builds the pinned six-case model-card
manifest (`examples.json`) with unchanged images, and `capture` runs
official Transformers 5.5.4 on one case to retain the reference
evidence. `processor` rewrites the committed fixtures in
`zig/src/families/glm_ocr/fixtures` without a GPU, and `attention`
writes the SDPA fixtures that `TF_GLM_OCR_ATTENTION_FIXTURES` names
for `zig/tests/hip/aotriton_test.zig`. See each subcommand's `--help`.

## Supported scope

The qualified path is BF16 on gfx1201, with one rank, up to four
independent shared lanes and exact verification windows through 32
rows. Copy drafts are supported; the checkpoint's separate MTP head,
tensor parallelism, fp8 KV, Sliding Weights and YaRN are not qualified
and their dedicated flags are refused. Custom HIP kernel-policy
profiles have not been qualified; use the settings above.

Prompt caching uses the shared core Store. Default retention is at
most 1 GiB after admitted lane/workspace storage, with the shared
snapshot-slot limit. Zero disables retention. A snapshot keeps one
keyed prepared row and the full prompt row count. A compatible resume
keeps that full row shape and skips vision work only for images wholly
inside its saved prefix. A different full prompt row count runs fresh
and logs `GlmOcrPromptShapeChanged`. Cache hits are visible in the
response's `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`.

Arbitrary shorter prompt chunks are not byte-identical to a full pass.
The implementation retains the full prompt arithmetic to preserve
fidelity. It does not claim arbitrary-cut arithmetic or changed-shape
cache reuse. On the qualified GPU, the original six examples, all
generated logits, positive cache resumes, shared lanes and copy drafts
showed zero output differences from the reference. Other hardware and
runtime versions need their own qualification.
# GLM target-row sampling checks

Use the version in `.zig-version` and the final PR head. Run one model process under the existing GPU lock
and admission guard. Keep the host's current load, context and cache budgets; do not increase them for this check.
This recipe qualifies sampling, separately from the cache lifetime repair in #835. It carries the shared-sampler
repair from #524; that PR's previous model receipts do not qualify this combined tree.

## Host and synthetic Metal checks

```sh
zig build native -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig build test test-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1
MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1 zig build test-glm-sampling -Dcpu=apple_m1
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/zig -p test_check_glm_sampling.py
zig fmt --check build.zig zig
python3 tools/zig/lean_check.py
```

Structured output and required tool calls need the release archive's `lib/` or `zig build grammar -Dxgrammar=DIR`; prepare DIR with `git clone --branch v0.2.8 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar` (use the native build's same `--prefix` for grammar).

The lean baseline is main `c7137bb3`: 527 findings. Compare identities with `tools/zig/lean_new.py`;
a nonzero checker result is not a clean run. Every new finding must be fixed.
The synthetic gate uses the actual shared `tf_sample_full` and production dispatch, including mixed and solo rows.

## Served model checks

Start the newly built native server using the existing admitted configuration and a public model name.
Replace `local-model` and the URL below with the values exposed by that server.

```sh
python3 tools/zig/check_glm_sampling.py http://127.0.0.1:8080 local-model --output glm-sampling-receipt.json
python3 tools/bench_concurrent.py http://127.0.0.1:8080 local-model --tokens 64 --reps 2 --temperatures 0,1 --levels 1,4 --alone --serial --output glm-concurrent-receipt.json
```

Require positive restored-token counts, native token hashes, drafted telemetry greater than zero, equality between
plain and drafted replies, and solo/concurrent equality with both draft modes. Report any cold/restored mismatch;
do not waive one because prompt chunk kernels can differ. Repeat with the MTP head omitted, using
`--skip-drafted-qualification` for the first client, and label that run as unqualified for drafting.
Cancel a streaming sampled reply, then repeat a known fresh request and compare its native token hash.

## Standalone depth-zero pipeline

Build `zig build tf-glm-run -Dcpu=apple_m1`. Supply public token arrays using the existing `PROMPTS_JSON` format
shown by `tf-glm-run`: `{"prompts":[{"name":"public-case","ids":[1,2,3]}]}`.
Use meaningful public prose/code token arrays from the checkpoint tokenizer for qualification.

```sh
GLM_SAMPLING=12,0.7,40,0.9,0.05 GLM_DEPTHS=0,3 GLM_MAX=64 GLM_CANCEL_TEST=1 zig-out/bin/tf-glm-run MODEL_DIR PROMPTS_JSON
GLM_SAMPLING=12,0,0,1,0 GLM_DEPTHS=0,3 GLM_MAX=64 zig-out/bin/tf-glm-run MODEL_DIR PROMPTS_JSON
```

Depth zero must exercise the pipelined plain rounds with sampled rules at each input position plus one.
Require identical token arrays at both depths, repeated-seed equality and cancellation followed by a valid fresh run.
Run with and without MTP where supported. Two-Mac sampled requests must still be refused before state changes;
check greedy peer behavior on two Macs when available.

Record the exact final commit, GPU/OS, checkpoint revision, runtime, public inputs, request settings and token hashes.
Include pass/fail/skip counts, before/after decode and cold prompt timings, and physical/device memory peaks.
Host checks and semantic compilation do not qualify device execution, model parity or performance.
# Living Weights keep-rate experiment (#1587)

Run this on the issue's untaught Nemotron 3.5 Lightning MLX 4-bit checkpoint with the base binary and the candidate binary.
Use the same backend, device, runtime libraries and build settings. Run it with exclusive use of the GPU.
The runner starts one server process at a time.

```sh
python3 tools/zig/keep_rate_ab.py \
  --base BASE_BINARY --candidate CANDIDATE_BINARY \
  --checkpoint CHECKPOINT --checkpoint-revision REVISION \
  --backend mlx --output NEW_RECEIPT_DIRECTORY
```

For a GB10 use `--backend cuda` and matching CUDA binaries/checkpoint. `--server-args` accepts a JSON argument
array, without a shell. Its default is `['--context','4096','--parallel','2','--temperature','0']` (use JSON double
quotes when overriding). Host, port, authentication, slide, seed-policy and thinking flags are managed by the
runner. It rejects overrides of those flags and quiet logging. It clears `TF_SLIDE_*` environment overrides for
both arms. Other runtime environment settings are inherited and must match; save them with the device receipt.
`--port`, `--startup-timeout` and `--request-timeout` can be supplied. Binaries must directly accept `serve MODEL`.

The fixed lesson is `{"text":"My favourite colour is teal."}` with no supplied wordings or explicit request seed.
Each binary runs ten fresh trials with `--prompt-seed` and ten without it, under default thinking and
`--no-thinking`: 40 lessons per arm, 80 total. The two arms alternate order between successive trials. Each trial
starts from its own independent checkpoint copy and empty graph. Clone/reflink copies may share physical pages
but never file inodes. The runner checks the copied file set and sizes and hashes the original before and after.
The input checkpoint must already be untaught; an empty metadata graph alone cannot prove that its weights are.

Each arm/mode/seed-policy cell first records a separate fresh `--slide`-off token baseline. Each lesson trial
records those same unrelated requests before and after teaching with `--slide` on, then restarts that copy with
`--slide` off and records them again. The controls ask three fixed unrelated questions greedily, with drafts off,
fixed request seeds and full generated token arrays, including reasoning tokens. Their requests use the server's
thinking default. Token IDs must be valid u32 values and match the server's hash when provided. Any mismatch is
reported. Sampled, drafted, concurrent and resumed serving comparisons remain separate device gates.

Receipts include binary and runner hashes, source checkpoint hashes/revision, commands, process IDs/exits, health,
complete server logs, raw lesson SSE, parsed events, graph snapshots, every parsed round and cumulative step count,
per-fact plain/thinking/probe counts, redraws and actual logged sampled-request seeds. Seed records name the
request and log line. A round also lists seeds logged since the preceding round; this includes writer and check
calls and does not pretend to identify a seed for a greedy request. Partial HTTP bodies and available round logs
are retained when a request fails. A stopped experiment's incremental results remain on disk.

Older base binaries lack the new counts. These are `null`, with `rounds_missing_counts` reported, never inferred
from the verdict or filled with zero. Missing candidate counts or absent round/seed logs fail the receipt.
Per-round `recalled` and `held_token_equal` preserve the server's own verdicts. Final keeps require a completed
stream, successful save, recalled learned events and a learned graph fact. This runner does not independently
reimplement the server's acceptance checks or establish that content seeding improves the real model.

`summary.json` includes every scheduled trial in each keep-rate denominator. Refusals remain in `results.json`
and their SSE files. Transport/protocol failures are errors, not invented refusals. A known lesson verdict remains
in the rate if a later measurement fails; the error count can overlap that known keep/refusal. Missing trials and
unresolved lessons are explicit. Exit zero means the protocol completed and recorded token controls agree, even
if every lesson was refused. It is not a release qualification or an improvement claim.

Checkpoint-copy hashes after each case list changed files. Copies are removed after recording unless
`--retain-copies` is supplied; use it when inspecting fitted neurons or failed restoration. Full weight hashing
and restart checks add experiment time. `lesson_seconds` measures only the learn HTTP request; `case_seconds`
also includes copy, startup, controls, restarts, hashing and cleanup. Keep logs and manifests for all attempts.

The host test launches only synthetic child HTTP servers with tiny fictional checkpoint files:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/zig -p test_keep_rate_ab.py -v
```

It executes the full 80-trial matrix and checks refusals, flags, raw receipts, exact tokens, restart controls,
original-file safety, unknown old counts, missing candidate diagnostics, truncated streams, HTTP errors and
occupied ports. It neither loads model weights nor opens a GPU driver. Real keep rates remain unmeasured here.
# Kimi K3 and capped K3.1 on native Metal

This is a resident adapter bring-up for synthetic components and a cut-down graph.
No real weights, no model-forward reference, no full-model run.
The complete released checkpoint does not run on one Mac through this adapter: admission prices every expert,
prepared projection, stream state, prompt cache and reserve before opening its weights, and refuses by budget.
There is no SSD residency path.

Build on a Mac with the Metal toolchain:

```sh
zig build native tf-k3-serve-check tf-k3-text-golden -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig-out/bin/tf-k3-serve-check
```

The native serving entry for an explicitly supplied local cut-down checkpoint is:

```sh
zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve LOCAL_CHECKPOINT --parallel 1 --context 2047 --prompt-cache-gib 0
```

This command is not a claim that the released checkpoint fits.
The directory needs its matching config, safetensors index and shards, `tiktoken.model`, and `tokenizer_config.json`.
Stored MXFP4 experts and BF16 projections retain the existing K3 geometry; synthetic fixtures may reduce layer,
expert and vocabulary counts.
K3.1 validates the released DSA config and refuses over 2047 total evaluated tokens, including restored prefix,
reply and speculative rows.
Its all-visible equivalence is inferred from our GLM implementation, not confirmed by a K3.1 model reference.
Prompt-state restore separately checks `max_ctx` before copying cache or logits.

The native text path uses release XTML segments and masked tiktoken encoding.
Thinking efforts are low, medium, high and max; thinking defaults to max effort when enabled.
Reasoning and complete calls to offered tools are read from actual added-token controls.
Ordinary spellings remain text, and raw completions retain generated XTML as text.
Images, external draft heads, TP, learning, disk states, required tool grammar, structured-output enforcement,
thinking budgets and answer-only limits are unsupported.

The K3.1 release license's Model-as-a-Service condition requires a separate Moonshot agreement for commercial use by operators whose aggregate affiliate revenue exceeds US$20 million over any consecutive 12 months, subject to its Section 4 exceptions; see [the supplied license](../../LICENSES/Kimi-K3.1-Pro.txt).

The prompt/value port and golden fixtures are credited in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../../THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
For an already available local tokenizer with the pinned release assets, run
`zig-out/bin/tf-k3-text-golden LOCAL_TOKENIZER_DIRECTORY` to compare all 15 release prompt ID arrays.
Synthetic tokenization checks do not replace that real-asset check or real-model qualification.
# Kolibri-1

This page describes the native engine. `kolibri1` serves Aleph Alpha's Kolibri-1, a research checkpoint, on one
NVIDIA GPU through the lane host. It is a draft family: plain decoding and copy drafts from the prompt's own text are
in; the EAGLE-3 drafter is the next step and is not loaded here.

## Checkpoint

Tested revision: `Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1` at `e52eb4627d11516b0c01de49210ab5a4e4061444` (32 shards, 74 GB). The
weights are block FP8: e4m3 codes in 128 x 128 blocks with fp32 `weight_scale_inv`, the routers, norms, embeddings and
head in bf16. Publisher sha256 of `model.safetensors.index.json`:
`c6769a34820c9057b404b2a5cae1ac24fd7b4a9ca08b84eb0a06e7b5bad3005e`.

```bash
tensorfold-native serve /path/to/Kolibri-1 --name kolibri-1 --context 32768 --parallel 8
```

The model has 50 layers, 2,560 wide, 48 query heads over 4 key heads of 128. Every fifth layer (4, 9, ..., 49) attends
to every key without positions; the other 40 attend to a 513-key window with RoPE. Each layer routes by sigmoid with an
expert bias to 6 of 384 experts, weighted by the unnormalised sigmoid, plus one ungated shared expert.

## What the family adds

It brings no kernels of its own. Every launch is a shared CUDA operator:

- `cuda/fp8.zig` and `qlinear` for the attention projections (block FP8, `fp8g` lane tiles);
- `cuda/experts.zig` for the routed and shared experts (`fp8g`, the shared expert stacked last at weight 1);
- `qk_rows` (QK norm, RoPE, the cache write), `norms`, `embed_rows`, `moe_glue` (sigmoid top-k with bias),
  `dense_rows` (router and head);
- `window_attention` for prompt rows of every layer (the full layers with no window) and for sliding decode rows;
- `tree_attention` for the full layers' decode rows over committed keys and each window's chain.

The family supplies its config check, the tensor map (116,303 tensors, none left over), the packing into those
layouts, the layer graph and the lane backend. One-row steps replay a CUDA graph a stream; wider windows and shared
rounds run eager. Both give a row the same bits.

## Serving

- Prompts run in passes of up to 8,192 rows, as the Python engine ran them, one a step, so other streams' rounds run
  between them (a full pass holds them for about 3.7 s). A row's bits do not depend on its chunk: 1,000-, 1,536- and
  2,048-row cuts of a 5,000- and a 20,000-token prompt give the 8,192-row passes' logits byte for byte.
- Concurrent streams share rounds of up to 64 rows. Each stream's caches are allocated at load, one per `--parallel`
  stream: at a 32k window 1.29 GiB a stream, at 64k 1.92 GiB. Each sliding layer's ring holds a pass and its window
  (8,768 keys).
- The prompt cache keeps a stream's state at any row: full layers' keys up to it and each sliding layer's last 512.
- Drafts: the lane core's copy drafts verify in windows of up to 16 rows. There is no draft head yet, so a request
  for head drafts and `--drafter` are refused by name.
- Refused at load: other quantizations, `norm_topk_prob`, other layer kinds, a config with a vision tower, shapes the
  shared kernels do not take, `--vision`, `--precision` and a captured kernel set (`TENSORFOLD_CUDA_KERNELS`).

## Checks

```bash
zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Dnvcc=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
zig-out/bin/tf-cuda-test kolibri-reference MODEL IDS   # layer 0 and the head against float64 from the checkpoint
zig-out/bin/tf-cuda-test kolibri-layers MODEL IDS      # the 513-key window edge, layer 4's full reach
zig-out/bin/tf-cuda-test kolibri-full MODEL IDS 128    # steps, drafted, sampled, shared rounds, cuts, kept states
zig-out/bin/tf-cuda-test kolibri-greedy MODEL PROMPTS N OUT   # greedy ids and top-2 margins a step
zig-out/bin/tf-cuda-test kolibri-logits MODEL IDS OUT  # teacher-forced logits of 2,048 rows, for quality
```

`IDS` is a file of real-text token ids (20,000 or more for `kolibri-full`, 3,000 for `kolibri-layers`). Random ids give
flat logits and say nothing about quality.

The native rows are not byte-equal to the Python engine's: its glue was Triton, these are the shared CUDA operators,
and their fp32 roundings differ by an ulp here and there. Kolibri-1's top-6-of-384 routing turns such differences into
different experts on near-tied rows, so greedy replies part where two tokens are nearly tied. On 2,048 rows of real
text, teacher-forced: next-token top-1 agrees on 92.3% of rows, KL 0.06; NLL 3.574 here against 3.578 for the
Python engine, top-1 35.96% against 35.47%, mean entropy 2.354 against 2.358.

## Speed

GB10, greedy, served by `tensorfold-native` with copy drafts on:

| | tok/s |
| --- | ---: |
| One stream, code / chat (`bench_openai.py`, 256 tokens) | 51.9 / 49.8 |
| 4 streams, aggregate | 124.0 / 126.0 |
| 8 streams, aggregate | 175.5 / 183.1 |

Cold prompts (`bench_cache.py --require-cold --repeats 3`, `--prompt-cache-gib 0`, median of the cold requests):
2,048 tokens 0.97 s, 8,192 tokens 3.72 s, 32,768 tokens 16.8 s, 64,000 tokens 37.8 s to the first token.

# LFM2.5-24B-A2B, native Metal and CUDA

This recipe covers [`LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit`](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit)
at revision `667408d494bde191c2cb9dd4f4549827816b9275`. The numbers below are measured on this 4-bit export only.

```bash
hf download LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-MLX-4bit \
  --revision 667408d494bde191c2cb9dd4f4549827816b9275 --local-dir "$HOME/models/lfm2.5-24b-a2b-4bit"
zig build native -Dcpu=apple_m1
zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve "$HOME/models/lfm2.5-24b-a2b-4bit" --port 8080 --parallel 16
```

A Mac with less memory may not hold 16 streams at the checkpoint's 131,072-token window; the server then names how
many fit. `--context 40960` holds 16 on a 48 GB M4 Pro.

## Shared rounds

Every stream's tokens go through the lane rounds. A round of several streams is one forward over all their rows.
In it each layer's short conv (30 layers) and each attention layer's qk, attention and merge (10 layers) run once
over every row (`lfm2_segments.metal`), from a table of each stream's cache addresses, row offsets and key counts
(`segments.zig`). Each row's arithmetic is the per-stream kernel's, so a reply equals its solo run. Prompt calls and
one-stream windows keep the per-stream launches. A greedy row takes the GPU's pick of its logits (`lfm2_argmax`);
sampled and masked rows draw on the host. The dense twin takes its MMA window only for matrices of 4,096 outputs or
more (the short conv's input and the head); narrower ones keep the scalar passes.

`zig build test-lfm2` runs the family's tests. `tf-kernel-contract --only lfm2` checks the shared-round kernels and
the pick, and `tf-lfm2-exact` compares windows and shared rounds with one-row decode on the real weights.

## Measured

Greedy, 256 tokens, 16 public prompts, a different one a stream, 3 reps in each of 3 alternated rounds on an M5 Ultra;
aggregate tok/s, the range of the rounds' medians. Before is main at 0d24ecb3 (each stream's own launches), after adds
the shared-round kernels on it. The M4 Pro is not yet measured on a quiet machine.

| Streams | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 258.5-259.2 | 266.5-267.7 |
| 4 | 483.5-486.5 | 565.2-566.1 |
| 8 | 551.5-551.9 | 732.2-735.6 |
| 16 | 660.7-661.9 | 922.5-923.5 |

Every reply was token for token equal before and after, and equal to its solo run and to `"draft": false`.
Cold prefill at 2k, 8k and 32k tokens and peak memory did not change.

## CUDA

`lfm2_moe` also serves the 4-bit export above (same revision, `667408d494bde191c2cb9dd4f4549827816b9275`) on one
NVIDIA GPU, through the lane host. Checked on a GB10 (sm_121).

```bash
zig build native -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -Dnvcc=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve "$HOME/models/lfm2.5-24b-a2b-4bit" --port 8080 --parallel 8
```

The default window is 32,768 tokens (`--context`), and `--parallel` holds up to 128 streams if the memory budget fits
them. Each stream has fixed pages for its keys and values. The family reads MLX affine 4-bit weights in groups of
64, with the embedding at 4, 6 or 8 bits. The 6- and 8-bit exports are refused by name and stay on Metal. Drafts
are the lane core's copy drafts from the prompt's own text; there is no draft head yet.

Most launches are shared CUDA operators: the affine linears and experts, the norms, `qk_rows`, the MoE combine, the
pick and the draws. The family adds three kernels: the router (fp32 weights, sigmoid plus bias, top-4) in
`lfm2_moe.cu`, and the 3-tap short conv and its state commit in `liquid_conv.cuh`. It also adds two instances of shared
templates at head dim 64: `pattn_kernel<64, 8, 4, 8>` for prompt rows, and `tf_paged_attn_chunk_segs_64` with
`tf_paged_attn_merge_segs_64` (`paged_attn_segs.cuh`) for decode rows. All of them are under the kernel contract
(see [the contract](../kernel-contract.md#coverage)).

Receipt (GB10, nvcc 13.0, `--parallel 8`, greedy):

- drafted == plain and concurrent == solo on 8 of 8 prompts, and the token hashes are the same after a restart;
- a float64 forward of the same weights on the CPU (`tools/lfm2_moe/ref64.py`) picks the engine's greedy token on
  421 of 435 teacher-forced prompt rows and 123 of 128 reply rows; `tools/lfm2_moe/REF64.md` lists every miss with
  both tokens and margins;
- decode, total tok/s: 87 at 1 stream, 194 at 4, 303 at 8;
- cold TTFT: 0.32 s at 2.8k prompt tokens, 1.32 s at 11.2k.

# LFM3 native Metal bring-up

Tracking issue: [#1491](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/issues/1491).

This slice implements native LFM3-1.7B text generation. LFM3-VL execution is in the dependent vision slice.
Both read the official MLX affine 4-, 6-, and 8-bit checkpoints without converting stored weights.
This is an experimental family port. Device and model checks cover an M4 Pro and an M5 Ultra; they do not qualify other Apple GPUs.

## Run the models

Build the native engine with the Zig version in `.zig-version` and Xcode's Metal toolchain:

```sh
zig build native -Dcpu=apple_m1
./zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native serve LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-MLX-4bit --context 8192
```

Replace `4bit` with `6bit` or `8bit` for those exports. A complete local checkpoint folder also works.
This slice refuses VL checkpoints until the vision contribution is applied.
Image budgets and decoder libraries are described by the stacked VL contribution.

The shared lane engine handles target verification, sampling and concurrent streams.
Convolution history and KV state are kept per stream; partial acceptance restores the accepted row's state.
Raw prompts of at least 256 tokens can build a repeat-cache entry: the first request records interest,
the second keeps a prefix state, and a later repeat resumes it. Image cache identity includes image content and grid.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  I[Image pixels] --> V[Vision encoder and projector]
  V --> E[Placeholder embedding rows]
  T[Text tokens] --> E
  E --> D[Shared LFM3 decoder]
  D --> L[Existing lane engine]
```

## Inspect a checkpoint

Use Python 3.11 or newer. The inspector uses the standard library. It resolves a full Hugging Face commit,
reads the config and index, and requests only the safetensors headers. It refuses a server that returns a
complete weight file instead of the requested byte range.

```sh
python3 tools/lfm3/inspect_checkpoint.py LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-MLX-4bit --output text4.json
python3 tools/lfm3/inspect_checkpoint.py LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B-MLX-4bit --output vl4.json
```

Replace `4bit` with `6bit` or `8bit` to inspect those exports. Pass `--revision COMMIT` to repeat a pinned inspection.
Use `--local-dir MODEL_DIR` instead of a repository name to inspect files already on disk.

## Check the native text layout

Use the Zig version in `.zig-version`.

```sh
zig build test-lfm3-host tf-lfm3-check
./zig-out/bin/tf-lfm3-check text4.json
./zig-out/bin/tf-lfm3-check vl4.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/lfm3 -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

The native checker reads the saved metadata, validates shard header geometry, and checks the LFM3 text decoder's
required names, dtypes, shapes, and byte counts. It performs no projection, GPU allocation, or model inference.
For VL, it checks the text decoder only. A passing result does not validate vision weights or image processing.

The config reader preserves full-attention versus sliding-attention layers, distinct rotary settings, sandwich norms,
and each module's affine width and group size. Unsupported geometry and conflicting quantization declarations fail.

## Checkpoint details

All six inspected MLX exports store the decoder under `language_model.model.*`, including the text-only model.
Each decoder has 594 tensors. Convolution kernels are BF16 with shape `[2048, 7, 1]`.

Text 4/6/8-bit and VL 6/8-bit use affine groups of 64. VL 4-bit uses groups of 32 and an 8-bit embedding override.
The 138 additional VL vision/projector tensors are BF16 in all three exports. Global quantization metadata must not
cause these dense tensors to be treated as packed affine weights.

The header inspections used these revisions:

- Text 4-bit: `d0ca73dcfa70ce18733754a492cdc1fb0123262d`.
- Text 6-bit: `26be898c36b545d625d84ac0761c6c3eb664aef3`.
- Text 8-bit: `ee7667f3cfccb2a41725f91820531823fcabc6b7`.
- VL 4-bit: `c823fade98e35a3d6942ad4d38b1ea15f675cd12`.
- VL 6-bit: `6d71bfae121abedc75f6d531fc7f6ceb4f5e3501`.
- VL 8-bit: `83336d5be3874a2bdd3297bde77b2114dbd3a816`.

## Qualification and remaining gate

Detailed counts, hashes, numerical evidence and reproducible requests are in the [receipts](../receipts/lfm3/README.md).

All six checkpoints passed 303 greedy/seeded-sampling, cache, concurrency and cancellation checks on one optimized M4 binary.
The final source build also passed 303/303 on an M5. Text4 and VL4 additionally passed real grammar, thinking, tool,
streaming, history and image-conditioned tool checks with the matching optional grammar library.
The 4-bit text long exactness suite passed all 73 cases through 8,193-token seams.
The final family contract passed 50 kernels and caught all 13 real controls, with zero limit problems.

Independent projection audits covered 66 class/layout cells and 60,954,624 outputs with no violations of existing FP32/BF16 bounds.
The row-pair optimization preserves the shared arithmetic: 132 checkpoint calls and a full 8,193-token logit comparison were byte-identical.
On the M5, controlled 4-bit cold requests improved text engine prefill from 1.240 to 0.813 seconds at 2k and
73.402 to 61.633 seconds at 64k; VL decoder requests improved from 1.262 to 0.815 and 73.920 to 59.647 seconds.
These are engine prefill measurements; the receipt also retains client TTFT. All compared full output-token hashes matched.

Native inference retains the checkpoint's BF16 activation boundaries and FP32 reductions.
Text trigonometric values round to BF16 before rotation; vision axial trigonometric values remain FP32.
The CPU FP64 oracle records numerical differences rather than inventing a tie policy.
MLX's vector/matrix quantized paths use different effective reconstruction, and bounded FP32 differences can propagate through history.
See the exact primitive and whole-model evidence before interpreting a next-token mismatch.

```sh
zig build tf-lfm3-forward tf-lfm3-vision tf-lfm3-project tf-lfm3-profile tf-lfm3-exact -Dcpu=apple_m1
./zig-out/bin/tf-lfm3-exact MODEL_DIR --long
python3 tools/lfm3/serve_check.py --binary ./zig-out/native/bin/tensorfold-native --model-dir MODEL_DIR --sampled --cancel --output served.json
```

Long-context model fidelity, maximum image budgets, 6/8-bit performance and other Apple GPU generations remain separate qualification work.
Structured output requires the native grammar library; logprobs and video are not advertised.
A complete earlier global M5 contract run found one Qwen4 failure that also reproduces on the unchanged pinned base.
It is not a final-source global pass. Agree model-fidelity and performance gates on #1491 before claiming release readiness.

## Weight licence

The official text and VL MLX exports retain the LFM Open License v1.0.
See the [text licence](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-MLX-4bit/blob/main/LICENSE) and
[VL licence](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-VL-2B-MLX-4bit/blob/main/LICENSE).
TensorFold code remains Apache-2.0. The measured Macs are M4 Pro 48 GB and M5 Ultra 256 GiB.
Receipts that include VL describe the combined chain, not a capability enabled in this text-only slice.
# LightOnOCR-3 on native HIP

The native HIP engine serves the three official BF16 sizes of
LightOnOCR-3 (0.8B, 1B and 4B). All three are qualified on gfx1201 only.
The 0.8B and 4B models use the Qwen3.5 family. The 1B model uses a Qwen3
text decoder and Pixtral vision encoder in `families/lighton_ocr`.
The legacy `mistral3` type is accepted only with the checked LightOnOCR
architecture and tensor shapes.

The implementation follows the existing ownership boundaries:

| Responsibility | Files |
| --- | --- |
| 1B config, image processor and weight admission | `zig/src/families/lighton_ocr/` |
| 1B Pixtral tower, Qwen3 text and lane backend | `zig/src/families/lighton_ocr/backend/hip/` |
| 0.8B/4B text loading and HIP engine | `zig/src/families/qwen3_5/` |
| Shared Qwen vision tower | `zig/src/vision/qwen_hip*.zig` |
| New HIP operators | `zig/kernels/hip/lighton_ocr.hip`, `qwen_vision.hip` |
| Native registration and image offer | `zig/src/native/hip.zig`, `hip_vision_offer.zig` |
| Device contracts | `zig/tests/hip/contract_lighton*.zig`, `contract_qwen*.zig` |
| Model capture and state checks | `zig/tests/lighton_hip/` |
| Pinned HF reference fixture capture | `tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py` |

Weights stay outside the checkout. The HIP loader widens BF16 weights to
FP32 without changing their values. Activations stay BF16. Allow room for
this storage, the vision tower, scratch buffers and each request's caches.
Do not change checkpoint files or add quantization metadata.

## Build and serve

Use Zig 0.17.0 and the local HIP compiler. Select the target GPU architecture
explicitly. This example uses a Radeon gfx1201 GPU.

```sh
zig build native-hip -Dhip=true -Dhip-arch=gfx1201 \
  -Dhipcc=/opt/rocm/core/bin/hipcc -j4
zig-out/native-hip/bin/tensorfold-native serve MODEL_DIRECTORY \
  --backend rocm --vision --context 4096 --parallel 2 --no-thinking \
  --name lighton --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8090
```

The 0.8B and 4B models load as `qwen3_5`, whose template opens a reasoning
block when `enable_thinking` is true. `--no-thinking` makes the server
default match the model cards, which render with `enable_thinking=False`;
a request can still set `chat_template_kwargs`. The 1B template has no
such switch, and its family declares no reasoning block.

JPEG inputs require the project's pinned libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1. Set
`TENSORFOLD_LIBTURBOJPEG` to that library when it is outside the normal
loader path. See [native preview](../../ZIG-PREVIEW.md) for image libraries.

For an isolated GPU test, identify the physical PCI address and acquire the
existing device lease. Shared tests must account for current users, the
complete planned allocation and a VRAM reserve. Set a process memory cap
and monitor remaining VRAM. Select the ROCm GPU UUID and verify that visible
HIP device 0 has that PCI address before loading. ROCm ordinals can differ
from `amd-smi` ordinals.

Use image-only user content for transcription. Add a text part containing
`grounding` for bounding boxes. Send images as OpenAI `image_url` data URLs.
PDF rendering belongs in the client. The family does not run a PDF parser.

## Reference examples and diagnostics

The model cards use this receipt in their Transformers examples:

[Official receipt fixture](https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/fixtures_ocr/resolve/28fe12cdf7816b5dde94e22051b2ec8dc74267b7/SROIE-receipt.jpeg).

Its SHA256 is
`d66a3287c847823c6ddab9f8b2080582b96a66b7816d178472f697ea84e227b3`.

`tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py` pins each checkpoint revision, the
SHA256 of every non-weight file in it, and the Transformers 5.22.1
model, processor and tokenizer sources each size loads. Every command
checks those pins before any model code runs. `sources` prints the
hashes and loads no model. `examples` runs the model card's
Transformers example on the receipt, in grounding and transcription
mode. It runs greedy and the card's own sampled call (1024 tokens,
`enable_thinking=False` on the 0.8B and 4B, temperature 0.2). It writes
a JSON receipt of prompt and output ids with their hashes:

```sh
python3 tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py sources --size 0.8B \
  --model MODEL_DIRECTORY
python3 tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py examples --size 0.8B \
  --model MODEL_DIRECTORY --image SROIE-receipt.jpeg \
  --output RECEIPT.json --device cuda:0
```

`tools/zig/lighton_ocr_pixels.py` checks the same 1B pins, then runs the
1B processor, called as the card does, on the 40 synthetic pages that
`zig/src/families/lighton_ocr/pixels_test.zig` makes. It prints each
page's CHW pixel shape and SHA256; the test holds those rows in
`fixtures/processor_pixels.txt` and compares its own prepared pixels
with them byte for byte:

```sh
python3 tools/zig/lighton_ocr_pixels.py --model MODEL_DIRECTORY \
  --output processor_pixels.txt
```

`tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py capture` writes processor pixels,
vision features, decoder inputs and teacher logits with pinned local
Transformers and checkpoint files. Outputs must be outside the checkout.
The script does not compare tensors. The HIP capture tools read those
fixtures, verify their checkpoint and tensor checksums and compare the
native tensors with the reference:

```sh
python3 tools/zig/lighton_ocr_reference.py capture --model MODEL_DIRECTORY \
  --size 1B --revision REVISION --expect-transformers-version VERSION \
  --image RECEIPT.jpeg --output REFERENCE --device cpu
zig build tf-lighton-hip-capture tf-qwen-hip-capture \
  tf-hip-kernel-contract -Dhip=true -Dhip-arch=gfx1201 \
  -Dhipcc=/opt/rocm/core/bin/hipcc -j4
zig-out/bin/tf-lighton-hip-capture MODEL_1B REFERENCE OUTPUT 0
zig-out/bin/tf-qwen-hip-capture MODEL_QWEN REFERENCE OUTPUT 0
zig-out/bin/tf-hip-kernel-contract image lighton_ocr full
zig-out/bin/tf-hip-kernel-contract image qwen_vision full
```
